Potato.source_title: AESA based IPM package for Potato (NIPHM, 2014)

pests.name: Aphid
pests.scientific_name: Myzus persicae Sulzer, Aphis gossypii Glover (Hemiptera: Aphididae)
pests.symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck sap from young leaves/shoots causing curling, stunting and honeydew-induced sooty mould; aphids also transmit potato virus Y (PVY) and potato leaf roll virus (PLRV).
pests.cultural_control: Use healthy seed, hot/cold weather cultivation, green manuring; plant early bulking/maturing cultivars in areas with short aphid-free periods.
pests.biological_control: Spray NSKE 5%; conserve parasitoids (Lysiphlebus sp, Diaeretiella sp, Aphelinus sp, Aphidius colemani) and predators (ladybird beetle, lacewing, spider, hover fly).
pests.chemical_control: carbofuran 3% CG @ 6.64 Kg/acre or oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 0.4 l in 200-400 l water/acre or thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 40 g in 200 l water/acre or phorate 10% CG @ 4 Kg/acre or soil drenching of thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 80 g in 200 l water/acre
pests.dosage: carbofuran 3% CG @ 6.64 Kg/acre; oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 0.4 l/200-400 l water/acre; thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 40 g/200 l water/acre (or 80 g/200 l as drench); phorate 10% CG @ 4 Kg/acre

pests.name: Jassid / leaf hopper
pests.scientific_name: Amrasca devastans Dist., Empoasca fabae Harris (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae)
pests.symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck plant sap causing leaves to curl, turn pale/bronze and dry up.
pests.cultural_control: Same common cultural practices as for aphid/thrips (healthy seed, timely irrigation, fertilizer management).
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids (Anagrus flaveolus, Stethynium triclavatum) and predators (lacewing, red ant, mirid bug, big-eyed bug, ladybird beetle).
pests.chemical_control: carbofuran 3% CG @ 1.328 Kg/acre for controlling leaf hopper
pests.dosage: carbofuran 3% CG @ 1.328 Kg/acre

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.symptoms: Causes chlorotic spots, yellowing, downward curling and drying of leaves; vector of potato leaf curl disease.
pests.cultural_control: Grow peppermint as a repellent plant for whitefly.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids (Encarsia formosa, Eretmocerus spp.) and predators (ladybird beetle, lacewing, spider, hover fly, reduviid bug, robber fly).
pests.chemical_control: Same as aphid control: carbofuran 3% CG @ 6.64 Kg/acre or oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 0.4 l/200-400 l water/acre or thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 40 g/200 l water/acre or phorate 10% CG @ 4 Kg/acre
pests.dosage: Same rates as listed for aphid control

pests.name: Thrips
pests.symptoms: Rasping/sucking causes reddish-brown/bronzy leaves, silken webbing under severe infestation, wilting and drying; also transmits viral diseases.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices; healthy seed use.
pests.biological_control: Spray NSKE 5%; conserve parasitoid Ceranisus menes and predators (predatory thrips, minute pirate bug, lacewing).
pests.chemical_control: dimethoate 30% EC @ 264 ml in 200-400 l water/acre for controlling thrips
pests.dosage: dimethoate 30% EC @ 264 ml/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Potato tuber moth
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into tubers and foliage causing irregular galleries/tunnels in tubers (especially in storage) and mined leaves; larval feces visible near bore holes.
pests.cultural_control: Intercrop cowpea/onion/maize/coriander/urdbean (1:2), rotate with non-host crops, plant seed tubers at 10 cm depth, ridge crop after 6-7 weeks so tubers stay buried 25 cm deep, timely irrigation to avoid soil cracking, proper curing and storage.
pests.biological_control: Inundative release of Trichogramma pretiosum @ 0.4 lakh/acre 4-5 times from flower initiation at weekly intervals; natural enemies include Chelonus blackburni, Copidosoma koehleri, Trichogramma spp.
pests.chemical_control: Managed primarily via cultural/biological practices; chemical control targets co-occurring pests (aphid/thrips insecticides) since tubers are protected by ridging and storage hygiene
pests.dosage: Trichogramma pretiosum @ 0.4 lakh/acre, 4-5 releases at weekly intervals from flower initiation

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.symptoms: Feeding causes leaf damage; regional pest of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Orissa.
pests.cultural_control: Grow flowering plants (carrot family, bishop's weed, sunflower family, French bean) to attract predatory mites/natural enemies.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predatory mites and predatory thrips.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately specified; follow common cultural, mechanical and biological practices

pests.name: Leaf miner
pests.symptoms: Larvae mine inside leaves; severe infestation leaves only upper/lower leaf skins, affected leaves dry and drop.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices.
pests.biological_control: Natural enemies: parasitoids Chrysocharis pentheus, Gronotoma micromorpha, Diglyphus isaea; predators lacewing, ladybird beetle, spider, red ant.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in this package

pests.name: Tobacco caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Larvae feed gregariously scraping chlorophyll (papery white appearance) then cause irregular holes and heavy defoliation.
pests.cultural_control: Grow castor as ovipositional trap crop.
pests.biological_control: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma pretiosum @ 20,000/acre/week (4 times); spray NSKE 5% against eggs/first instar larvae; apply entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) @ 2,50,000 infective juveniles of Steinernema feltiae/sq mt.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed; controlled via biological measures listed
pests.dosage: Trichogramma pretiosum @ 20,000/acre/week x4; EPN Steinernema feltiae @ 2,50,000 IJ/sq mt

pests.name: Leaf eating caterpillar / gram pod borer
pests.symptoms: Caterpillars scrape leaf lamina giving papery white appearance, then make irregular holes; heavy defoliation.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices.
pests.biological_control: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma pretiosum @ 20,000/acre/week (4 times); spray NSKE 5%; apply EPNs @ 2,50,000 infective juveniles of Steinernema feltiae/sq mt.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

pests.name: Cutworm
pests.scientific_name: Agrotis segetum Denis & Schiffermuller (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) - regional
pests.symptoms: Larvae sever stems of young plants at night, pulling parts into ground; can cause boreholes on tubers larger than potato tuber moth damage.
pests.cultural_control: Attract larvae with rice bran heaps placed in field in late afternoon then destroy next day; flood field prior to planting where possible.
pests.biological_control: Natural enemies: Trichogramma spp., Tetrastichus spp., Telenomus spp., Bracon spp., Campoletis spp., Chelonus spp., Ichneumon spp., Carcelia spp.; predators lacewing, ladybird beetle, spider, red ant, dragonfly, robber fly, reduviid bug, praying mantis, King crow.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in this package

pests.name: White grub / root grub
pests.scientific_name: Lachnosterna longipennis Blanchard, L. coracea (Coleoptera: Scarabaeidae) - regional
pests.symptoms: Grubs feed on rootlets/roots then tubers; second/third instar grubs make large shallow circular holes in tubers (more than two holes often per tuber).
pests.cultural_control: Follow common cultural, mechanical and biological practices.
pests.biological_control: Entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) sprayed @ 1 billion nematodes/acre in infested fields, or EPN-infected Galleria/Corcyra cadavers implanted @ 4 cadavers/plant during May/June and/or September.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed
pests.dosage: EPN @ 1 billion nematodes/acre or 4 infected cadavers/plant

pests.name: Root-knot nematode
pests.symptoms: Root swelling, irregular tuber shape with lumps, stunting, early maturity, wilting under hot conditions; warty pimple-like outgrowths on tubers.
pests.cultural_control: Plant in 2nd week of October (autumn) or early January to limit infestation; grow one row of repellent African marigold (Tagetes patula, T. erecta) between 2-3 rows of potato.
pests.biological_control: Apply NSKE 4% and neem cake @ 80 Kg/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Managed mainly by cultural/biological methods in this package
pests.dosage: neem cake @ 80 Kg/acre

pests.name: Cyst nematode (golden nematode)
pests.scientific_name: Globodera rostochiensis (Wollenweber), Globodera pallida (Stone) - regional (Tamil Nadu, Kerala)
pests.symptoms: Patches of poorly growing, temporarily wilting/stunted plants with premature yellowing; small mustard-seed-sized yellow/white female cysts visible on roots.
pests.cultural_control: Raise African marigold in nursery 15 days prior to sowing; use raised beds >35 cm height.
pests.biological_control: Apply neem cake @ 80 Kg/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Bacterial wilt
diseases.symptoms: Plant wilts from leaf tips/branch points, leaves yellow at base then whole plant wilts and dies; cut stems/tubers show brown ring which exudes white fluid; soil sticks to tuber eyes at harvest.
diseases.cultural_control: Use pathogen-free tubers; disinfect cutting knife with 1% sodium hypochlorite; apply lime (dolomite) as extreme soil pH is unfavourable to pathogen.
diseases.chemical_control: Two to three sprays of (streptomycin sulphate 9% + tetracycline hydrochloride 1%) SP @ 40 to 50 ppm solution at 20-day interval, first spray 30 days after planting
diseases.dosage: (streptomycin sulphate 9% + tetracycline hydrochloride 1%) SP @ 40-50 ppm, 2-3 sprays at 20-day interval

diseases.name: Septoria leaf spot
diseases.scientific_name: Septoria lycopersici var. malagutii Ciccarone & Boerema
diseases.symptoms: Small round-to-irregular spots with grey centre and dark margin on lower leaves progressing upward; spots coalesce causing blighting and defoliation.
diseases.cultural_control: Manage nutrient deficiency; avoid persistent moist conditions where possible.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the crop-stage table (managed with common practices)

diseases.name: Late blight
diseases.symptoms: Leaves appear blistered/scalded, rot and dry, turning brown/black; underside of leaves shows flour-like spore growth; stems blacken from tips; can kill plants within 2-3 days if uncontrolled; tubers show dry brown skin/flesh spots.
diseases.cultural_control: Use short-duration varieties; disease predicted when 7-day moving sum of RH >85% for 90+ hrs coincides with 7-day moving sum of temperature 7.2-26.6 degC for 115+ hrs.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified (Trichoderma/Pseudomonas used generally as seed/soil treatment)
diseases.chemical_control: captan 50% WG @ 600 g/200 l water or captan 50% WP @ 1 Kg/300-400 l water or captan 75% WP @ 666 g/400 l water or chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 350-500 g/240-320 l water or copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 1 Kg/300-400 l water or copper sulphate 2.62% SC @ 400 ml/200 l water or cyazofamid 34.5% SC @ 80 ml/200 l water or dimethomorph 50% WP @ 400 g/300 l water or mancozeb 75% WG @ 400 g/200 l water or mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/300 l water or hexaconazole 2% SC @ 1.2 l/200 l water or mandipropamid 23.4% SC @ 0.2 ml/l in 200-300 l water/acre or propineb 70% WP @ 300 g/100 l water or zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/300-400 l water or captan 70% + hexaconazole 5% WP @ 200-400 g/200 l water or cymoxanil 8% + mancozeb 64% WP @ 600-800 g/200-300 l water or famoxadone 16.6% + cymoxanil 22.1% SC @ 200 ml/200-300 l water or fenamidone 10% + mancozeb 50% WDG @ 500-600 g/200 l water or metalaxyl-M 4% + mancozeb 64% WP @ 0.25% (1 Kg/acre) in 200-400 l water or metalaxyl 8% + mancozeb 64% WP @ 0.25% (1 Kg/acre) in 400 l water or metiram 55% + pyraclostrobin 5% WG @ 600-700 g/200 l water or azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 200 ml/200 l water; tuber treatment with carbendazim 25% + mancozeb 50% WS @ (1.5+3.0) to (1.75+3.5) g/10 Kg seed tuber
diseases.dosage: See chemical_control field for full list of exact product rates as quoted from source (each an alternative spray option)

diseases.name: Early blight
diseases.symptoms: Small black lesions on older foliage first, enlarging with concentric rings in a bull's-eye pattern; surrounding tissue may yellow; high temperature/humidity kills much foliage; similar stem lesions can girdle plant near soil line.
diseases.cultural_control: Removal of infected debris; crop rotation.
diseases.chemical_control: aureofungin 46.15% w/v SP @ 0.005% in 300 l water/acre or captan 50% WG @ 600 g/200 l water or captan 50% WP @ 1 Kg/300-400 l water or captan 75% WP @ 666 g/400 l water or chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 350-500 g/240-320 l water or copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 1 Kg/300-400 l water or mancozeb 35% SC @ 0.5% or mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/300 l water or hexaconazole 2% SC @ 1.2 l/200 l water or kitazin 48% EC @ 0.20% (200 ml/200 l water) or propineb 70% WP @ 300 g/100 l water (0.30%) or zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/300-400 l water or captan 70% + hexaconazole 5% WP @ 200-400 g/200 l water
diseases.dosage: See chemical_control field for full list of exact product rates as quoted from source

diseases.name: Common scab
diseases.symptoms: Pathogen infects developing tubers via lenticels/wounds causing cork-like lesions; rough cracked skin with scab-like spots; severe infection leaves rough black welts.
diseases.cultural_control: Use healthy tubers, treat seed tubers with 3% boric acid for 30 minutes before/after cold storage; maintain optimum soil moisture from tuber initiation; rotate with wheat, peas, oats, barley, lupin, soybean, sorghum, bajra, green manure crops.
diseases.chemical_control: Spray thiram 75% WS @ 25 g/l water (second spray after 7-10 days interval)
diseases.dosage: thiram 75% WS @ 25 g/l water

diseases.name: Black scurf / canker
diseases.symptoms: Fungal bodies contact stolons causing stolon blinding (reduced tuber production/yield); tubers show black scurf, which is cosmetic (reduces appearance, not yield).
diseases.cultural_control: Soak seed tubers in trisodium phosphate (90 g/l water) one day before sowing, rinse and dry in shade; tubers stored in oxygen-deficient structures should not be used.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified beyond general Trichoderma/Pseudomonas seed treatment
diseases.chemical_control: Treat tuber with M.E.M.C. 6% FS @ 0.415 g/Kg tubers in 100 ml water for 3-5 minutes or soak seed tubers in streptocycline 40-100 ppm solution for half an hour prior to planting or carbendazim 25% + mancozeb 50% WS @ (1.5+3.0) to (1.75+3.5) g/10 Kg seed tuber or carboxin 37.5% + thiram 37.5% DS @ (1.5+3.0) to (1.75+3.5) g/10 Kg seed tuber
diseases.dosage: M.E.M.C. 6% FS @ 0.415 g/Kg tubers; streptocycline 40-100 ppm soak; carbendazim+mancozeb WS @ (1.5+3.0)-(1.75+3.5) per 10 Kg seed; carboxin+thiram DS @ (1.5+3.0)-(1.75+3.5) per 10 Kg seed

diseases.name: Viral diseases (Potato virus X, S, Y)
diseases.scientific_name: Potato virus X (PVX, Potexvirus), Potato virus S (PVS, Carlavirus), Potato virus Y (PVY, Potyvirus)
diseases.symptoms: PVY causes stipple streak and necrosis in susceptible varieties; PVS causes vein deepening, rough leaves, mild mottling; PVX often symptomless or causes chlorosis/mosaic/necrotic tuber lesions; combined infections cause more severe symptoms and yield loss.
diseases.cultural_control: Use healthy certified seed; control aphid vectors.
diseases.biological_control: Same as aphid/thrips biological control (NSKE 5% spray)
diseases.chemical_control: Managed via vector (aphid) control - same insecticides as listed under Aphid

diseases.name: Potato Spindle Tuber Viroid (PSTVd)
diseases.symptoms: Mild foliar symptoms with smaller leaves curling downward giving upright growth habit, stunting, grey distorted leaves; tubers become narrow/spindle-shaped with prominent eyebrows, may crack or develop knobs.
diseases.cultural_control: Use certified virus/viroid-free planting material; avoid mechanical transmission via tools.
diseases.chemical_control: No chemical control (viroid); manage via sanitation and certified seed

diseases.name: Black leg and soft rot
diseases.symptoms: Black leg is rot of lower stem encouraged by cool damp conditions; soft rot occurs when bacteria enter tuber through wounds, dissolving cell walls and liquefying tuber (no distinct smell in true soft rot).
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid physical damage to tubers during harvest/handling to prevent post-harvest rot entry points.
diseases.chemical_control: Not chemically treated in this package; managed by sanitation/handling

diseases.name: Pink rot
diseases.symptoms: Foliar wilting and chlorosis from underground infection; tubers infected via diseased stolons show darkened skin, rotted tissue remains firm/slightly spongy; cut tuber tissue oxidizes to pinkish tinge.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid high soil moisture and cool conditions that favour disease; use disease-free seed.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Black heart (physiological disorder)
diseases.scientific_name: Acute oxygen deficiency (abiotic disorder, not a pathogen)
diseases.symptoms: Blackening of tuber centre from acute oxygen deficiency in storage (low temperature confined storage or high field soil temperature); tissue dies from inside out turning jet black, no smell; affected tubers rot later.
diseases.cultural_control: Maintain cold storage at 4 degC or slightly higher with proper aeration.
diseases.chemical_control: Not applicable

Potato.general_safety_precautions: Do's/Don'ts include: do not apply pesticides during the 7 days preceding harvest; do not spray at midday (most insects inactive); spray undersides of leaves thoroughly especially for mites/whitefly/Spodoptera; do not apply chemical pesticides within 7 days of parasitoid release; apply NPV/SlNPV only in the evening on early instar larvae, never during the day; store pheromone lures refrigerated, not at room temperature; use short-persistence pesticides to avoid residues in soil/produce. Toxicity classes noted for pesticides used include: Carbofuran (Class Ib, extremely toxic), Phorate (Class Ib, extremely toxic), Dimethoate (Class II, highly toxic - antidote atropine), Oxydemeton-methyl (Class III, moderately toxic), Endosulfan (highly toxic), Thiamethoxam (Class III, moderately toxic).
Potato.waiting_period_notes: Harvesting interval (days) given for pesticides in the safety-parameters table: Endosulfan 3 days; Dimethoate 6 days; Oxydemeton-methyl 6 days; Thiamethoxam 6 days; Carbofuran and Phorate not specified (--) in the table. General rule: avoid applying any pesticide during the 7 days before harvest. For seed potatoes, apply chlorpropham 50% HN antisprouting agent @ 36-40 ml/MT under cold storage; treat seed tubers with 3% boric acid solution for 30 minutes before storage to protect against black scurf/common scab.

Maize.source_title: Integrated Pest Management Package for Maize (NIPHM/DPPQS)

pests.name: Maize stem borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into whorls/stems causing dead hearts (drying of central shoot).
pests.cultural_control: Deep summer ploughing followed by fallowing; intercropping with legumes (maize-soybean/maize-cowpea/maize-green gram) reduces borer incidence; removal and destruction of dead hearts.
pests.biological_control: Release Trichogramma chilonis @ 1,60,000/ha on 7 and 15 day old crop, weekly thereafter; conserve Cotesia flavipes, carabids, coccinellids, Chrysoperla, spiders, wasps.
pests.chemical_control: Granular application of Carbofuran 3% CG on infested plant whorls @33.3 kg/ha for borer, shoot fly and thrips (10-15 days after germination) or spray Carbaryl 85% WP @ 1764 g/l against borer at 15-18 days after germination
pests.dosage: Carbofuran 3% CG @ 33.3 kg/ha (whorl application); Carbaryl 85% WP @ 1764 g/l

pests.name: Pink stem borer
pests.symptoms: Similar boring damage to stem borer causing dead hearts.
pests.cultural_control: Same as maize stem borer: crop rotation, intercropping with legumes, deep summer ploughing.
pests.biological_control: Release of Trichogramma chilonis @ 1,60,000/ha.
pests.chemical_control: Same as stem borer: Carbofuran 3% CG @ 33.3 kg/ha or Carbaryl 85% WP @ 1764 g/l
pests.dosage: Carbofuran 3% CG @ 33.3 kg/ha

pests.name: Shoot fly
pests.symptoms: Maggots damage growing shoot causing dead hearts in seedling stage.
pests.cultural_control: Balanced plant spacing (75x18 cm kharif, 60x18 cm rabi); balanced NPK fertilization.
pests.biological_control: Not specifically listed for shoot fly beyond general Trichogramma releases
pests.chemical_control: Granular application of Carbofuran 3% CG @ 33.3 kg/ha in whorls or spray Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 625 ml/ha or Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1155 ml/ha or Oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 1000 ml/ha or Phorate 10% CG @ 30 Kg/ha
pests.dosage: Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 625 ml/ha; Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1155 ml/ha; Oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 1000 ml/ha; Phorate 10% CG @ 30 Kg/ha

pests.name: White grub
pests.symptoms: Grubs damage roots underground.
pests.cultural_control: Collection and destruction of white grub stages during pre-sowing deep ploughing; manual collection/destruction of adults during emergence period.
pests.biological_control: Soil application of neem cake for control of nematode and chafer beetle.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed for white grub specifically in this package

pests.name: Cyst nematode
pests.scientific_name: Heterodera zeae Koshy et al. (regional: Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar)
pests.symptoms: Root infestation reduces vigor; damage assessed by cyst counts per gram soil (ETL 3-4 cysts/g soil).
pests.cultural_control: Deep summer ploughing 2-3 times at 10-15 day intervals (April-May) with summer fallowing and weed destruction; use non-cereal crops (vegetables, oilseeds, pulses) when 3 cysts/g soil; use moderately resistant variety Ageti-71.
pests.biological_control: Apply neem cake @ 50 kg/ha; organic amendments - combined mustard cake and tobacco dust @ 2.5 q/ha.
pests.chemical_control: Soil application of Carbofuran 3% CG @ 2.0 kg a.i./ha (at 4 cysts/g soil)
pests.dosage: Carbofuran 3% CG @ 2.0 kg a.i./ha

diseases.name: Turcicum leaf blight (TLB)
diseases.symptoms: Leaf blight lesions reducing photosynthetic area; national significance disease.
diseases.cultural_control: Use resistant varieties (PEMH-5, Vivek 21/23/25, Pratap Kanchan 2, Nithyashree for Karnataka/Andhra); sanitation and crop rotation.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified beyond Trichoderma seed treatment for related stalk rots
diseases.chemical_control: Foliar spray at first appearance of leaf blight with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1.5 to 2 kg/l of water, followed by 2-4 applications at 10 days interval if needed
diseases.dosage: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1.5-2 kg/l water, repeat at 10-day intervals

diseases.name: Maydis leaf blight (MLB)
diseases.scientific_name: Drechslera maydis (Niskado & Miyake) Syn. H. maydis
diseases.symptoms: Leaf blight symptoms similar to TLB.
diseases.cultural_control: Use resistant varieties (HM10, PAU 352, Malviya Hybrid Makka 2, PEMH1, HQPM series, Shaktiman 3/4).
diseases.chemical_control: Same fungicide regime as TLB - Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1.5-2 kg/l water
diseases.dosage: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1.5-2 kg/l water

diseases.name: Common rust / Polysora rust
diseases.scientific_name: Puccinia sorghi Schw. (common rust); Puccinia polysora Underw. (Polysora rust, regional)
diseases.symptoms: Pustules on leaves reducing photosynthetic area and yield.
diseases.cultural_control: Use resistant varieties (Buland, Sheetal, HHM1, HHM2, HQPM1, Nithyashree; Nithyashree for Polysora rust in AP/Karnataka).
diseases.chemical_control: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1.5 to 2 kg/l of water or Zineb 75% WP @ 1.5-2 kg/ha at first appearance of pustules, three sprays at 15 days interval if needed
diseases.dosage: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1.5-2 kg/l water OR Zineb 75% WP @ 1.5-2 kg/ha, 3 sprays at 15-day interval

diseases.name: Banded leaf and sheath blight
diseases.scientific_name: Rhizoctonia solani f. sp. sasakii Exner
diseases.symptoms: Banded lesions on leaf sheaths spreading upward.
diseases.cultural_control: Stripping of 2 lower leaves along with leaf sheath; resistant varieties (Pratap Kanchan 2, Pratap Makka 3/5, Shaktiman 1/3).
diseases.biological_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum 2.0% WP @ 20 g/kg of seeds.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed beyond biological seed treatment
diseases.dosage: Trichoderma harzianum 2.0% WP @ 20 g/kg seed

diseases.name: Downy mildews (Brown stripe, Sorghum, Rajasthan downy mildew)
diseases.scientific_name: Sclerophthora rayssiae var. zeae Payak & Renfro (brown stripe); Peronosclerospora sorghi Weston & Uppal Shaw (sorghum); Peronosclerospora heteropogoni Siradhana et al. (Rajasthan)
diseases.symptoms: Systemic downy mildew symptoms reducing vigor; regional diseases in Himachal Pradesh/Uttarakhand/Punjab, Karnataka/Tamil Nadu, and Rajasthan respectively.
diseases.cultural_control: Plant before rainy season begins; avoid maize-sorghum rotation/adjacency for sorghum downy mildew; rogue and destroy infected plants and alternate host Heteropogon grass for Rajasthan downy mildew; use resistant varieties (PEMH5, Bio9636, NECH-X1280, DMH1, NAC6002, COH(M)4/5).
diseases.chemical_control: Seed treatment with fungicide Metalaxyl 35% WS @ 0.75 to 1.0 g/100 kg seed in endemic areas; foliar spray of Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1.5-2 kg/l at very first appearance of symptoms
diseases.dosage: Metalaxyl 35% WS @ 0.75-1.0 g/100 kg seed

diseases.name: Pythium stalk rot
diseases.symptoms: Pre-flowering stalk rot.
diseases.cultural_control: Plant population not to exceed 50,000/ha; good field drainage; removal of previous crop debris/wheat straw.
diseases.chemical_control: Seed treatment with fungicide Metalaxyl-M 31.8% ES @ 2.4 ml/kg of seed
diseases.dosage: Metalaxyl-M 31.8% ES @ 2.4 ml/kg seed

diseases.name: Bacterial stalk rot
diseases.scientific_name: Erwinia chrysanthemi p.v. zeae (Sabet) Victoria, Arboleda & Munoz.
diseases.symptoms: Stalk rot associated with water logging.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid water logging, proper drainage, planting on ridges, avoid sewage water for irrigation.
diseases.chemical_control: Soil drenching of bleaching powder containing 33% chlorine @ 10 kg/ha at pre-flowering stage

diseases.name: Fusarium stalk rot (post-flowering)
diseases.symptoms: Post-flowering stalk rot.
diseases.cultural_control: Sanitation/removal of previous crop debris; lower plant population; balanced soil fertility (avoid high N, low K); crop rotation with soybean.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in this package (managed culturally)

diseases.name: Charcoal rot
diseases.symptoms: Stalk rot worsened by moisture stress at flowering.
diseases.cultural_control: Sanitation, deep ploughing, avoid water stress at flowering, balanced fertility.
diseases.biological_control: Add Trichoderma harzianum formulation 2.0% WP in furrows at sowing, mixed with FYM @ 10 g/kg FYM, incubated 10 days in moist condition.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Late wilt
diseases.symptoms: Wilt disease associated with moisture stress.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid moisture stress, balanced potash application, avoid planting seed from infected areas, rotation with other crops.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

Maize.general_safety_precautions: Follow classification of toxicity per Insecticides Rules 1971 and WHO hazard classification with colour toxicity triangle guidance; extension functionaries should educate farmers via toxicity triangle colours and ensure doctors near spraying areas have pesticide labels/leaflets for antidote procurement. Use appropriate PPE, purchase only required quantity, store away from food/children, never transfer to other containers, avoid carrying pesticides with food materials.
Maize.waiting_period_notes: No crop-specific harvesting-interval table was found in this package; general safety Annexures (IV, V, IX) cover pesticide toxicity classification, basic precautions and symptoms/treatment of poisoning applicable to the insecticides/fungicides listed (Carbofuran, Carbaryl, Dimethoate, Endosulfan, Monocrotophos, Oxydemeton-methyl, Phorate, Mancozeb, Metalaxyl, Thiram, Zineb).

pests.name: Gram pod borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into fruits/shoots causing damage; national significance pest in Karnataka.

pests.chemical_control: Seed treatment with thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 7 g/kg seed; foliar spray emamectin benzoate 5% SG @ 80 g in 200 l water/acre or fipronil 5% SC @ 320-400 ml in 200 l water/acre or flubendiamide 39.35% SC @ 40-50 ml in 200 l water/acre or indoxacarb 14.5% SC @ 133-160 ml in 120-240 l water/acre or lufenuron 5.4% EC @ 240 ml in 200 l water/acre or spinosad 45% SC @ 64 ml in 200 l water/acre or novaluron 10% EC @ 150 ml in 200 l water/acre or chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 60 ml in 200 l water/acre or deltamethrin 2.8% EC @ 160-200 ml in 160-240 l water/acre or lambda-cyhalothrin 4.9% CS @ 200 ml in 200 l water/acre or methomyl 40% SP @ 300-450 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or thiodicarb 75% WP @ 250.4-400 g in 200 l water/acre or indoxacarb 14.5% + acetamiprid 7.7% SC @ 160-200 ml in 200 l water/acre or pyriproxyfen 5% + fenpropathrin 15% EC @ 200-300 ml in 200-300 l water/acre

pests.name: Aphids

pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Aphidius colemani, Diaeretiella spp., Aphelinus spp.; predators Orius spp., mirid bugs, syrphid flies, green lacewings, coccinellids (Stethorus punctillum), staphylinid beetle, Aphidoletis aphidimyza, Feltiella minuta.

pests.name: Yellow mite / other mites
pests.scientific_name: Polyphagotarsonemus latus Banks (Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka); Tetranychus spp.
pests.symptoms: Causes leaf curling/bronzing and stunting; national significance.
pests.cultural_control: Border chilli crop with two rows of maize per 0.5 acre.

pests.dosage: See chemical_control field for exact rates

pests.name: Root-knot nematode
pests.symptoms: Root galling reducing plant vigor.
pests.cultural_control: Deep summer ploughing; soil solarization with 45-gauge polythene for 3 weeks before sowing.
pests.biological_control: Apply neem cake @ 100 kg/acre at transplanting.
pests.chemical_control: In severe nematode areas apply carbofuran 3% CG granules @ 26,640 g/acre
pests.dosage: carbofuran 3% CG @ 26,640 g/acre

diseases.name: Damping off
diseases.symptoms: Seedling collapse in nursery beds, especially under excessive watering/poor drainage.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid excessive watering/poorly drained areas; use raised beds >15 cm height; raise seedlings in pro-trays/plug trays.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified beyond general Trichoderma/Pseudomonas seed and nursery treatment
diseases.chemical_control: Seed treatment with captan 75% WS @ 25-30 g/kg seed; soil drenching with captan 75% WP @ 1000 g in 400 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: captan 75% WS @ 25-30 g/kg seed; captan 75% WP @ 1000 g/400 l water/acre (soil drench)

diseases.name: Choanephora blight
diseases.symptoms: Blight affecting flowers/fruits especially under dense canopy with poor air circulation.
diseases.cultural_control: Adopt recommended spacing for air circulation; grow resistant varieties.
diseases.chemical_control: Spray captan 75% WP @ 800 g in 400 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: captan 75% WP @ 800 g/400 l water/acre

diseases.name: Die back and fruit rot (anthracnose)
diseases.symptoms: Dieback of shoots and fruit rot; spreads via infected planting material and water stagnation.
diseases.cultural_control: Use healthy pathogen-free seed; early removal of affected plants; control weeds/solanaceous volunteers near transplant houses; avoid water stagnation, ensure good field drainage.
diseases.chemical_control: For die back and fruit rot: benomyl 50% WP @ 80 g in 240 l water/acre or captan 75% WP @ 800 g in 400 l water/acre or copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 1000 g in 300-400 l water/acre or difenoconazole 25% EC @ 50 ml in 200 l water/acre or hexaconazole 2% SC @ 1200 ml in 200 l water/acre or propineb 70% WP @ 200 g in 200-300 l water/acre or tebuconazole 25% WG @ 200-300 g in 200 l water/acre or zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300-400 l water/acre or azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 200 ml in 200-300 l water/acre or chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 320 g in 300 l water/acre or kitazine 48% EC @ 80 ml in 200-300 l water/acre or mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300 l water. For anthracnose and fruit rot: captan 50% WG @ 600 g in 200 l water/acre or captan 70% + hexaconazole 5% WP @ 200-400 g in 200 l water/acre or copper sulphate 2.62% SC @ 400 ml in 200 l water/acre or copper hydroxide 77% WP @ 500 ml in 200 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: See chemical_control field for full list of exact product rates

diseases.name: Mosaic complex (viral)
diseases.scientific_name: Mixed virus complex (aphid-transmitted) - Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, UP, Maharashtra
diseases.symptoms: Mosaic mottling of leaves, stunting, reduced yield; aphid-vectored.
diseases.cultural_control: Select healthy seed; crop rotation with non-hosts; control perennial weed hosts; rogue infected plants early; grow tolerant varieties; raise 4 rows of maize/sorghum as border crop against aphid vectors; cover seedbed with nylon net or paddy straw.

diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on leaves.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified
diseases.chemical_control: Spray dinocap 48% EC @ 90 ml in 300 l water/acre or fenarimol 12% EC @ 40 ml in 200-300 l water/acre or flusilazole 40% EC @ 40-60 ml in 200 l water/acre or sulphur 52% SC @ 800 ml in 160 l water/acre or sulphur 80% WP @ 1252 g in 300-400 l water/acre or azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 200 ml in 200-300 l water/acre or benomyl 50% WP @ 80 g in 240 l water/acre or hexaconazole 2% SC @ 1200 ml in 200 l water/acre or tebuconazole 25% WG @ 200-300 g in 200 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: See chemical_control field for exact rates

diseases.name: Cercospora leaf spot
diseases.symptoms: Circular leaf spots reducing photosynthetic area.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified
diseases.chemical_control: Spray mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300 l water or zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300-400 l water/acre or copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 1000 g in 300-400 l water/acre or benomyl 50% WP @ 80 g in 240 l water/acre or copper hydroxide 77% WP @ 500 ml in 200 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: See chemical_control field for exact rates

diseases.name: Bacterial leaf spot
diseases.symptoms: Leaf spots of bacterial origin; spreads via infected seed.
diseases.cultural_control: Field sanitation important; obtain seeds from disease-free plants/healthy fruits.
diseases.chemical_control: Spray streptomycin sulfate 9% + tetracycline hydrochloride 1% SP solution (streptocycline) @ 40-100 ppm after appearance of first true leaves; two sprays, one before transplanting (nursery) and one after (main field)
diseases.dosage: streptocycline 40-100 ppm, two sprays (nursery + main field)

diseases.name: Fusarium wilt
diseases.scientific_name: Fusarium solani (Mart.) Sacc. (Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh)
diseases.symptoms: Wilting of plants due to vascular infection.
diseases.cultural_control: Crop rotation, resistant varieties, field sanitation (general practice implied)
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the crop-stage table

Chilli.general_safety_precautions: Insecticide resistance management: use insecticides only as last resort when P:D ratio unfavourable (>2:1); rotate insecticide classes/modes of action; avoid broad-spectrum insecticides where narrow-spectrum will work; apply at recommended rates/timing per label.
Chilli.waiting_period_notes: Nutritional deficiency section notes Ca deficiency (blossom end rot) corrected by foliar calcium chloride spray. No separate crop-specific pre-harvest interval table was captured in the extracted sections; general practice per Do's/Don'ts across NIPHM packages is to avoid pesticide application in the final 7 days before harvest.

Groundnut.source_title: Integrated Pest Management Package for Groundnut (NIPHM)

pests.name: Aphid
pests.symptoms: Sap-sucking causes curling/stunting; vector of peanut bud necrosis virus.
pests.cultural_control: Stray planting of cowpea as trap crop.

pests.chemical_control: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 2 ml/kg seed or spraying Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 100-125 ml/500 lit water; soil application of Phorate 10% CG @ 15-25 kg/ha; need-based application of Dimethoate 0.05% or Monocrotophos 0.05% or Imidacloprid 0.008% or Dichlorovos 76% SC

pests.name: Bruchids
pests.symptoms: Damage to stored/harvested pods.
pests.cultural_control: Harvest at optimum maturity; dry pods to ~7% kernel moisture; store in polythene-lined gunny bags.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: In case of bruchid infestation, fumigate with Aluminium phosphide one tablet (3 g)/30 kg bag under air-tight conditions

pests.name: Jassid
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking causes hopper-burn symptoms on leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices with two hand hoeings.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Soil application of Phorate 10% CG @ 15-25 kg/ha for aphids and jassid; need-based Dimethoate 0.05% or Monocrotophos 0.05% or Imidacloprid 0.008%
pests.dosage: Phorate 10% CG @ 15-25 kg/ha

pests.name: Leaf miner
pests.symptoms: Larvae mine leaves reducing photosynthetic area; damages foliage during vegetative to flowering stages.
pests.cultural_control: Stray planting of soybean as trap crop.
pests.biological_control: Release of Trichogramma chilonis (50,000/ha) twice against leaf miner and other defoliators.
pests.chemical_control: Spray Dimethoate 30% EC @ 470-940 g/500-1000 lit water for controlling the leaf miner
pests.dosage: Dimethoate 30% EC @ 470-940 g/500-1000 l water

pests.name: Termite
pests.symptoms: Damage to seedlings and roots, especially in drought-stressed crop.
pests.cultural_control: Soil application of castor or neem cake @ 250 kg/ha.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Seed treatment with Chlorpyriphos 20% EC @ 2.5 to 12.5 ml/kg seed in endemic areas; soil application of Phorate 10% CG @ 15-25 kg/ha or Carbofuran 3% CG @ 33.3 kg/ha
pests.dosage: Chlorpyriphos 20% EC @ 2.5-12.5 ml/kg seed; Carbofuran 3% CG @ 33.3 kg/ha

pests.name: Thrips
pests.scientific_name: Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood, Thrips palmi Karny
pests.symptoms: Rasping-sucking damage to leaves; vector of tobacco streak virus causing peanut stem necrosis disease.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices; timely sowing to avoid vector buildup.
pests.biological_control: Not specified beyond general predator conservation
pests.chemical_control: Need-based application of Dimethoate 0.05% or Monocrotophos 0.05% or Imidacloprid 0.008% or Dichlorovos 76% SC for managing sucking pests
pests.dosage: See chemical_control field

pests.name: Tobacco caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Gregarious larval defoliation.
pests.cultural_control: Stray planting of castor and sunflower as trap crops; continue light trap/bonfire, mechanical collection of egg masses/larvae; install 5 pheromone traps/ha for monitoring or 25 traps/ha for mass trapping.
pests.biological_control: Release egg parasitoid Telenomus remus @ 50,000/ha (4 times, 7-10 day interval); spray S. litura NPV @ 250 LE (6x10^9/LE)/ha or Bacillus thuringiensis @ 1 kg/ha.
pests.chemical_control: Spray Quinalphos 1.5% DP @ 2300-2500 g/ha or Quinalphos 25% EC @ 1400 ml/ha or Dichlorovos 76% EC @ 470-940 ml/ha or Chlorpyriphos 20% EC @ 1 l/ha to control full-grown hairy caterpillar; Quinolphos 25% EC 0.05% or Chlorpyrifos 20% EC for managing defoliators like Spodoptera and Helicoverpa
pests.dosage: Quinalphos 1.5% DP @ 2300-2500 g/ha; Quinalphos 25% EC @ 1400 ml/ha; Chlorpyriphos 20% EC @ 1 l/ha

pests.name: Red hairy caterpillar / Bihar hairy caterpillar
pests.scientific_name: Amsecta albistriga Walker & A. moorei Buttler (red hairy caterpillar); Spilosoma/Diacrisia obliqua (Bihar hairy caterpillar) - regional
pests.symptoms: Larval defoliation, especially early in crop.
pests.cultural_control: Partial/complete lopping of host trees to reduce adult congregation; installation of 12 light traps/ha or bonfire in endemic areas; collection/destruction of egg masses.
pests.biological_control: Same as tobacco caterpillar: NPV, Bt.
pests.chemical_control: Spray Quinalphos 1.5% DP @ 2300-2500 g/ha or Quinalphos 25% EC @ 1400 ml/ha or Dichlorovas 76% EC @ 470-940 ml/ha or Chlorpyriphos 20% EC @ 1 l/ha
pests.dosage: See chemical_control field

pests.name: White grub
pests.scientific_name: Lachnosterna (Holotrichia) serrata Fab. and L. (Holotrichia) consanguinea Blanchard
pests.symptoms: Grubs damage roots.
pests.cultural_control: Partial/complete lopping of preferred host trees; collection/destruction of adults; crop rotation with wheat, maize, sorghum, pearl millet, cotton, onion/garlic.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Spraying white grub-harbouring host trees with Chloropyrifos 1.0-1.25 l/500-1000 l water; seed treatment with Chlorpyriphos 20% EC @ 2.5 to 12.5 ml/kg seed; soil application of Phorate 10% CG @ 15-25 kg/ha or Carbofuran 3% CG @ 33.3 kg/ha
pests.dosage: Chloropyrifos 1.0-1.25 l/500-1000 l water; Carbofuran 3% CG @ 33.3 kg/ha

diseases.name: Leaf spot (Early/Late Leaf Spot)
diseases.scientific_name: Phaeoisariopsis personata Berk. & Curt. and Cercospora arachidicola Hori.
diseases.symptoms: Leaf spots reducing photosynthetic area (ELS/LLS complex, national significance).
diseases.cultural_control: Rogue affected plants; crop rotation.
diseases.biological_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 10 g/kg seed; soil application Trichoderma viride @ 10 kg/ha multiplied in 250 kg FYM.
diseases.chemical_control: Two sprays of Difenaconazole 25% EC @ 100 ml/100 lit water or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 500 g/750 lit water or Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1500 ml/500 lit water at 15-day interval after disease appearance
diseases.dosage: Difenaconazole 25% EC @ 100 ml/100 l water; Propiconazole 25% EC @ 500 g/750 l water; Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1500 ml/500 l water

diseases.name: Rust
diseases.symptoms: Rust pustules on leaves reducing yield.
diseases.cultural_control: Same as leaf spot management.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified beyond Trichoderma seed treatment
diseases.chemical_control: Two sprays of Difenaconazole 25% EC @ 100 ml/100 lit water or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 500 g/750 lit water or Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1500 ml/500 lit water at 15 day interval for leaf spots and rust

diseases.name: Stem rot / Collar rot / Dry root rot
diseases.scientific_name: Sclerotium rolfsii Sacc. (stem/pod rot); Aspergillus niger Tiegh. (crown/collar rot); Rhizoctonia bataticola Taub. (dry root rot)
diseases.symptoms: Rotting at stem base/roots leading to plant collapse.
diseases.cultural_control: Deep summer ploughing; crop rotation; removal of previous crop residue.
diseases.biological_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 10 g/kg seed; soil application Trichoderma viride @ 10 kg/ha in 250 kg FYM 15 days prior to application at sowing.
diseases.chemical_control: Two sprays of Difenaconazole 25% EC @ 100 ml/100 lit water or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 500 g/750 lit water or Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1500 ml/500 lit water at 15 days interval
diseases.dosage: Trichoderma viride @ 10 g/kg seed; Difenaconazole/Propiconazole/Hexaconazole as above

diseases.name: Alpha-root (aflatoxin-associated)
diseases.symptoms: Pod rot and aflatoxin contamination, worse under immature/over-matured harvest and improper storage.
diseases.cultural_control: Harvest at optimum maturity (neither immature nor over-matured); dry pods to ~7% kernel moisture; store in polythene-lined gunny bags on raised platform (bags not sealed/stitched).
diseases.chemical_control: No chemical control recommended at maturity stage to avoid pesticide residues in harvested produce

diseases.name: Alternaria blight
diseases.scientific_name: Alternaria spp. / A. arachidis Kul. (rabi-summer groundnut)
diseases.symptoms: Blight lesions on leaves in rabi-summer season crop.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified beyond general disease practices
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Peanut bud necrosis disease (PBND) / Peanut stem necrosis disease
diseases.scientific_name: Peanut bud necrosis tospovirus / Tobacco streak virus (vector: Thrips spp.) - regional (Anantapur, A.P.)
diseases.symptoms: Bud necrosis and stem necrosis symptoms transmitted by thrips vectors.
diseases.cultural_control: Early sowing to avoid vector buildup (where irrigation available, except in endemic areas); dense cropping (increased seed rate) to reduce bud necrosis damage.
diseases.chemical_control: Managed through vector (thrips) control - see Thrips entry

Groundnut.general_safety_precautions: At maturity stage, no chemical control is recommended (Pod rot, leaf spots, rust, pod borers, termites, rodents, aflatoxins) to avoid pesticide residues in the harvested produce; only rodenticide (0.005% Bromadiolone cake) permitted at this stage.
Groundnut.waiting_period_notes: Store pods only after drying to ~7% kernel moisture in polythene-lined (unsealed) gunny bags on a raised platform to avoid Aspergillus flavus/aflatoxin buildup. Bruchid-infested stored bags may be fumigated with Aluminium phosphide 1 tablet (3g)/30 kg bag under air-tight conditions - standard fumigant safety/re-entry precautions apply.

Sugarcane.source_title: AESA based IPM package for Sugarcane (NIPHM)

pests.name: Early shoot borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into shoots causing dead hearts with foul smell.
pests.cultural_control: Deep summer ploughing, inter-culture and hand weeding, timely irrigation, light earthing up 3 months after planting, grow onion/garlic/coriander as intercrop, mulching in ratoon crop.
pests.biological_control: Release 125 gravid females of Sturmiopsis inferens (tachinid parasitoid) per acre; release Trichogramma chilonis @ 20,000/acre at 10-day interval at incidence.
pests.chemical_control: Fipronil 5% SC @ 600-800 ml in 200 l water/acre or Fipronil 0.3% GR @ 30-40 kg in water/acre or Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 500-600 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 150 ml in 400 l water/acre or Cypermethrin 10% EC @ 260-304 ml in 200-280 l water/acre or Quinalphos 5% granule @ 2000 g/acre or Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR @ 7.5 g/acre or Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 600-900 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or Quinalphos 25% EC @ 800 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: See chemical_control field for exact per-product rates

pests.name: Top shoot borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into top shoots causing dead hearts/damage.
pests.cultural_control: Collection/destruction of adult moths, egg masses, dead hearts; pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre; light trap @ 1/acre.
pests.biological_control: Release Trichogramma spp. @ 20,000/acre, 2-3 times at 10-day interval.
pests.chemical_control: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 150 ml in 400 l water/acre or Phorate 10% CG @ 12,000 g/acre or Carbofuran 3% CG @ 26,640 g/acre or Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR @ 7.5 Kg/acre
pests.dosage: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 150 ml/400 l water/acre; Phorate 10% CG @ 12,000 g/acre; Carbofuran 3% CG @ 26,640 g/acre

pests.name: Root borer
pests.symptoms: Boring damage to roots/base of shoot causing dead hearts.
pests.cultural_control: Same as early shoot borer practices.
pests.biological_control: Same as early shoot borer (Trichogramma, Sturmiopsis).
pests.chemical_control: Same chemical options as early shoot borer/top shoot borer

pests.name: Internode borer / Stalk borer / Plassy borer
pests.scientific_name: Chilo sacchariphagus indicus (Kapur) - internode borer; Chilo auricilius Dudgeon - stalk borer
pests.symptoms: Boring inside internodes/stalks.
pests.cultural_control: Proper water management to avoid lodging; de-trashing/removal of water shoots monthly from 5th month; balanced fertilizer doses; pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre.
pests.biological_control: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 20,000/acre, six releases at fortnightly intervals from 4th month.
pests.chemical_control: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 500-600 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 750 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 500-600 ml/200-400 l water/acre; Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 750 ml/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: White woolly aphid
pests.symptoms: Colonies suck sap producing white waxy woolly masses on leaves; weakens plant.
pests.cultural_control: De-trashing of infested canes; paired row planting; avoid excess nitrogen; do not transport infested tops; infested canes should not be used as planting material.
pests.biological_control: Conserve/augment natural enemies; promote entomopathogens Cladosporium oxysporum, Metarhizium anisopliae, Verticillium lecanii, Beauveria bassiana.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed primarily culturally/biologically

pests.name: Black bug
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking pest of sugarcane.
pests.cultural_control: Not separately specified
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Quinalphos 25% EC @ 800 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Quinalphos 25% EC @ 800 ml/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Scale insect
pests.symptoms: Scale colonies suck sap reducing vigor.
pests.cultural_control: Use resistant/tolerant varieties; select healthy pest-free setts; keep fields/bunds weed-free; avoid water stagnation and repeated ratoons; detrash at 150th and 210th day of planting.
pests.biological_control: Release coccinellid predators.
pests.chemical_control: Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 600 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 600 ml/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Pyrilla
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking causing honeydew/sooty mould and leaf drying.
pests.cultural_control: Avoid late nitrogen application; collect and cage egg masses to facilitate parasitoid emergence; remove/destroy lower dried leaves.
pests.biological_control: Release 3,200-4,000 cocoons or 3.2-4.0 lakh eggs of Epiricania melanoleuca per acre when 3-5 Pyrilla/leaf observed; conserve/augment Epiricania population.
pests.chemical_control: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 600 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or Dichlorvos 76% EC @ 150.4 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 200 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 600 ml/200-400 l water/acre; Dichlorvos 76% EC @ 150.4 ml/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Mealybug
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking colonies on cane, reducing vigor.
pests.cultural_control: Use resistant/tolerant varieties; de-trashing and removal of water shoots; drain excess water, avoid water stress.
pests.biological_control: Conserve/augment natural enemies (Chilocorus, Hyperaspis, Chrysoperla, Aphytis, Coccophagus, Encarsia).
pests.chemical_control: Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 600 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 600 ml/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.symptoms: Nymphs/adults feed on sap causing decline in vigor.
pests.cultural_control: Clip infested leaves; avoid water stress/water logging and low land planting; synchronize planting/harvest zone-wise; detrash puparia-bearing leaves and burn/bury; yellow sticky traps.
pests.biological_control: Conserve/augment Encarsia sp, Eretmocerus spp., mirid bug, dragonfly, spider, robber fly, praying mantis, fire ants, coccinellids, lacewings, big-eyed bugs.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed via cultural/mechanical/biological control

pests.name: Termite
pests.symptoms: Damage to setts/roots causing poor establishment.
pests.cultural_control: Remove stubble/debris of previous crop; dig termitaria and destroy queen; locate/destroy termite colony and affected setts.
pests.biological_control: Entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) sprayed @ 100 million nematodes/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 200-250 ml in 400 l water/acre or clothianidin 50% WDG @ 100 g in 400 l water/acre or imidacloprid 70% WS @ 28-42 g in 40-60 l water/acre or imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 140 ml in 750 l water/acre or chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 2.5 l/acre
pests.dosage: See chemical_control field for exact rates

diseases.name: Red rot
diseases.symptoms: Spindle leaves (3rd & 4th) dry; stalks discolour and become hollow with black acervuli on rind/nodes; split stalks emit sour smell with reddened internal tissue and intermingled transverse white spots. Spreads rapidly in rainy season, potentially destroying entire crop.
diseases.cultural_control: Use resistant/moderately resistant varieties (e.g., BO 128, Co 89029, CoH 2201, CoSe 92423, CoSe 95422); discard any sett showing reddening at cut ends/nodal region; remove affected clumps with roots and burn; bund affected fields to prevent floodwater spread; avoid ratooning diseased crop; harvest diseased crop early; crop rotation.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed (managed primarily through resistant varieties and sanitation)

diseases.name: Wilt
diseases.scientific_name: Acremonium implicatum (Gilman & Abbott) Gams; Fusarium moniliforme sub sp. glutinans J. Sheld.
diseases.symptoms: Gradual yellowing/drying of foliage, shrinkage of canes externally; internally light-to-dark purplish/brown discolouration of ground tissue with pithiness and boat-shaped cavities in internodes.
diseases.cultural_control: Use disease-free healthy setts; crop rotation; avoid over/flood irrigation in affected areas.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Grassy shoot disease
diseases.symptoms: Proliferation of vegetative buds from cane base giving crowded bunches of tillers with narrow, pale-yellow to chlorotic leaves; canes rarely form, and if formed are thin with short internodes.
diseases.cultural_control: Use disease-free setts; avoid ratooning diseased crop; yellow sticky traps for aphid vector control; disinfest cutting tools.
diseases.chemical_control: Managed via vector control (aphid, leafhopper) - use yellow sticky traps for aphid vector

diseases.name: Smut
diseases.scientific_name: Ustilago scitaminea (Syd.) M. Piepenbr., M. Stoll & Oberw.
diseases.symptoms: Whip-like structure (25-150 cm) emerges from growing point, covered by translucent silvery membrane enclosing black powdery spore mass; canes become thin with elongated internodes then reduced length; profuse lateral bud sprouting especially in ratoon.
diseases.cultural_control: Use resistant varieties (e.g., Co 8371, Co 85004, Co 86032, Co 86249, Co 87025); remove diseased clumps and burn; crop rotation; avoid ratooning diseased crop.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Leaf scald
diseases.symptoms: Can remain latent before symptoms appear; pencil-line white streaks with yellow borders along veins leading to necrosis; leaf areas become pale green/chlorotic ('scald').
diseases.cultural_control: Use disease-free setts; avoid stress conditions (drought, waterlogging, low temperature) that increase severity; disinfest tools/implements.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Red striped disease
diseases.symptoms: Chlorotic lesions with dark red stripes (0.5-1.0 mm wide) on leaves that may coalesce causing wilting/drying; whitish bacterial ooze flakes on lower leaf surface; young shoots show top/shoot rot with dark red discolouration of tissue when split.
diseases.cultural_control: Use disease-free setts, sanitation.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

Sugarcane.general_safety_precautions: Insecticide resistance management principles apply (rotate chemical classes, use as last resort at P:D ratio >2:1, apply per label rates/timing). Rodent management: bromadiolone 0.25% CB @ 0.005% or bromadiolone 0.005% RB @ 0.005% near burrows; avoid repeated use in same season to prevent bait shyness.
Sugarcane.waiting_period_notes: Note explicitly states pesticide dosages and spray fluid volumes are based on high-volume sprayer application; no specific crop pre-harvest interval table was captured for sugarcane in the extracted sections. Post-harvest: avoid trash burning to preserve natural enemies; destroy stubble in borer/white-grub infested fields.

Banana.source_title: AESA based IPM package for Banana (NIPHM)

pests.name: Banana rhizome weevil
pests.symptoms: Grubs tunnel into rhizome/pseudostem base reducing plant vigor and bunch weight.
pests.cultural_control: Removal of pseudostems below ground level; trimming rhizome; prune side suckers monthly; avoid susceptible varieties (Robusta, Karpooruvally, Malbhog, Champa, Adukkar); grow less susceptible Poovan, Kadali, Kunnan, Poomkalli.
pests.biological_control: Not specified beyond general predator conservation
pests.chemical_control: Before planting, dip suckers in carbofuran 3% CG @ 33 g/sucker then shade dry 72 hrs before planting; soil incorporation of carbofuran 3% CG @ 33 g/sucker at planting; pheromone lure ('cosmolure') traps @ 2/acre for monitoring/trapping
pests.dosage: carbofuran 3% CG @ 33 g/sucker

pests.name: Banana stem weevil
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into pseudostem causing tunnelling and plant weakness.
pests.cultural_control: Remove dried leaves periodically; prune side suckers monthly; use healthy pest-free suckers; do not dump infested material in manure pit; uproot/chop/burn infested trees; use longitudinally split pseudostem traps @ 26/acre.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed beyond general carbofuran use for rhizome pests

pests.name: Banana leaf eating caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Larvae defoliate leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Collect/destroy egg masses and caterpillars; burning torch for congregating larvae; summer ploughing to expose pupae; grow Ocimum/basil as repellent.
pests.biological_control: Field release of egg parasitoids Telenomus spodopterae, T. remus; conserve larval parasitoids Ichneumon promissorius, Carcelia spp., Campoletis chlorideae; predators Chrysoperla zastrowi sillemi, coccinellids, King crow, braconid wasp, dragonfly, spider, robber fly, reduviid bug, praying mantis, red ants; conserve nematode Ovomermis albicans.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed via mechanical (hand-picking, pheromone/light traps @ 4-5/acre) and biological control

pests.name: Banana aphid
pests.symptoms: Sap-sucking; vector of banana bunchy top disease.
pests.cultural_control: Yellow pan water sticky trap @ 4-5/acre; clean cultivation.
pests.biological_control: Encourage predator coccinellids (Scymnus, Chilomenes sexmaculatus) and lacewing Chrysoperla zastrowi sillemi.
pests.chemical_control: carbofuran 3% CG @ 166 g/sucker or dimethoate 30% EC @ 594-792 ml in 600-800 l water/acre or oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 1200-1600 ml in 600-800 l water/acre, directed toward crown and pseudostem base
pests.dosage: carbofuran 3% CG @ 166 g/sucker; dimethoate 30% EC @ 594-792 ml/600-800 l water/acre; oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 1200-1600 ml/600-800 l water/acre

pests.name: Banana lacewing bug / tingid bug
pests.symptoms: Damages leaves, flowers and fruits.
pests.cultural_control: Collect and destroy damaged leaves/flowers/fruits.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Spray carbofuran 3% CG @ 166 g/sucker or dimethoate 30% EC @ 594-792 ml in 600-800 l water/acre or oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 600-800 ml in 600-800 l water/acre, directed toward crown and pseudostem base
pests.dosage: carbofuran 3% CG @ 166 g/sucker; dimethoate 30% EC @ 594-792 ml/600-800 l water/acre

pests.name: Banana thrips
pests.symptoms: Damage to leaves, flowers, fruits.
pests.cultural_control: Blue pan water sticky traps @ 4-5/acre; destroy volunteer plants/old plantations; hot water treatment of suckers; bunch covers.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predators coccinellid and lacewings.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

pests.name: Hard scale
pests.symptoms: Scale colonies damage plant parts.
pests.cultural_control: Collect/destroy affected plant parts.
pests.biological_control: Field release of coccinellid predators Chilocorus nigritus, Cryptolaemus montrouzieri (Symnus coccivora).
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

pests.name: Fruit fly
pests.symptoms: Damage to ripening fruit.
pests.cultural_control: Grow less susceptible variety; physical barrier by bagging/wrapping fruits (double-layer newspaper/brown paper); collect/destroy fallen, damaged, overripe fruits; fruit fly trap every 20 m; early harvesting.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed (managed via bagging and trapping)

diseases.name: Sigatoka leaf spot
diseases.symptoms: Leaf spot lesions reducing photosynthetic surface.
diseases.cultural_control: Remove/destroy affected leaves; prevent water accumulation around plant; periodic weeding; select tolerant varieties (Ney Poovan, Pachanadan, Karpuravalli, Fhia 1/Gold finger, Sannachenkadali).
diseases.chemical_control: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 400 l water/acre or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 0.1% (100 ml/100 l water) in 200-400 l water/acre or Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 1 Kg in 300-400 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/400 l water/acre; Propiconazole 25% EC @ 100 ml/100 l water

diseases.name: Moko disease
diseases.symptoms: Bacterial wilt of banana.
diseases.cultural_control: Ensure good drainage; disinfest tools with formaldehyde diluted 1:3 with water; crop rotation (3 years with sugarcane or rice); fallow or flooding during off-season.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed (managed culturally)

diseases.name: Banana bunchy top disease (BBTD)
diseases.scientific_name: Bunchy top virus / Banana virus-1 / Musa virus-1
diseases.symptoms: Bunchy, stunted growth from stacked narrow leaves; aphid-vectored.
diseases.cultural_control: Select suckers from disease-free areas; destroy infected plants with 4 ml of 2,4-D (50 g in 400 ml water); remove weeds attractive to aphids; select tolerant varieties (Poovan, Pachanadan).
diseases.chemical_control: Control aphid vector by spraying carbofuran 3% CG @ 166 g/sucker or dimethoate 30% EC @ 594-792 ml in 600-800 l water/acre or oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 1200-1600 ml in 600-800 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: Same as banana aphid control

diseases.name: Panama wilt (Fusarium wilt)
diseases.scientific_name: Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cubense (E.F.Sm.) W.C.Snyder & H.N. Hansen
diseases.symptoms: Vascular wilt disease.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid susceptible cultivars (Rasthali, Monthan, Red banana, Virupakshi); grow resistant Poovan; remove/destroy affected leaves and spray BM (1%) + linseed oil (2%); select tolerant Dwarf Cavendish, Robusta, Fhia 1, Anai komban, Nivedya Kadali.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed; managed via resistant cultivars and sanitation

diseases.name: Tip rot
diseases.symptoms: Rot at fruit tip.
diseases.cultural_control: Remove and destroy infected plants.
diseases.chemical_control: Drench with mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 400 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/400 l water/acre

diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.scientific_name: Colletrotrichum musae Green & Goos, Gloeosporium musarum Cke. & Massee
diseases.symptoms: Post-harvest fruit rot.
diseases.cultural_control: Proper sanitation of handling equipment and prompt cooling to 14 degC minimize disease incidence in cold storage.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed (managed via cold-chain sanitation)

diseases.name: Cigar end rot
diseases.scientific_name: Verticillium theobromae (Turconi) E.W. Mason & S. Hughes - regional
diseases.symptoms: Fruit tip rot resembling a burnt cigar end, worsened in storage.
diseases.cultural_control: Prompt cooling to 14 degC; proper sanitation of handling facilities.
diseases.chemical_control: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 400 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/400 l water/acre

diseases.name: Infectious chlorosis
diseases.symptoms: Chlorosis of leaves.
diseases.cultural_control: Destroy infected plants; use disease-free suckers; dry heat treatment of suckers at 40 degC for 1 day; avoid growing cucurbits as intercrop.
diseases.chemical_control: Control aphid vector by applying carbofuran 3% CG @ 166 g/sucker or dimethoate 30% EC @ 594-792 ml in 600-800 l water/acre or oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 1200-1600 ml in 600-800 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: Same as banana aphid control

diseases.name: Banana bract mosaic virus / streak mosaic
diseases.symptoms: Mosaic symptoms on bracts/leaves.
diseases.cultural_control: Dry heat treatment of suckers at 40 degC for 1 day; avoid growing cucurbits as intercrop.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Finger tip / black tip rot
diseases.scientific_name: Botryodiplodia theobromae Pat. (Karnataka, Bihar, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh)
diseases.symptoms: Fruit tip blackening/rot.
diseases.cultural_control: Wrap banana fruit bunch in plastic bag prior to hot water dip.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

Banana.general_safety_precautions: Insecticide resistance management guidance applies (rotate modes of action, use as last resort, apply per label). Bagging fruit bunches and hot water treatment of suckers/fruit used as key non-chemical safety measures for storage pests/diseases.
Banana.waiting_period_notes: Note states pesticide dosages and spray fluid volumes are based on high-volume sprayer application. Cold storage/handling sanitation (14 degC prompt cooling) is emphasized as the primary post-harvest safety measure rather than chemical treatment for anthracnose/cigar end rot.

Soyabean.source_title: Integrated Pest Management Package for Soybean (NIPHM/DPPQS)

pests.name: Stem fly
pests.symptoms: Maggots cause seedling mortality by tunnelling into stems.
pests.cultural_control: Recommended seed rate (65-75 kg/ha); balanced NPK+S fertilization.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Seed treatment with Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 10 ml/kg seed to prevent seedling mortality (also controls whitefly transmitting YMV); spray Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 10 l/ha at 10-15 days after germination if heavy mortality expected
pests.dosage: Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 10 ml/kg seed (treatment) / 10 l/ha (spray)

pests.name: Girdle beetle
pests.symptoms: Adult girdles stem causing drooping and drying of leaves/shoots above the girdle.
pests.cultural_control: Manually remove infested plants/parts below girdles when drooping/drying observed.
pests.biological_control: Not specified beyond general Bt use for defoliators
pests.chemical_control: Spray Triazophos 40% EC @ 625 ml/ha or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 150 ml/ha, effective if applied within 7-10 days of girdling symptoms
pests.dosage: Triazophos 40% EC @ 625 ml/ha; Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 150 ml/ha

pests.name: Tobacco caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Gregarious larvae defoliate leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Collect/destroy gregarious larvae and egg masses; install pheromone traps @ 10/ha; install bird perches @ 8-10/acre.
pests.biological_control: Trichogramma chilonis, Tetrastichus, Telenomus (egg parasitoids); larval parasitoid, Carcelia spp.; Diglyphus isaea (larval); watch for natural Beauveria bassiana infection causing larval mortality.
pests.chemical_control: Spray Indoxacarb 15.8% EC @ 333 ml/ha for heavy incidence (do not repeat same insecticide for second spray); Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 150 ml/ha for mixed populations with Helicoverpa/semilooper
pests.dosage: Indoxacarb 15.8% EC @ 333 ml/ha; Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 150 ml/ha

pests.name: Green semiloopers
pests.scientific_name: Chrysodeixis acuta Walker, Gesonia gemma, Diachrysia orichalcea
pests.symptoms: Loopers defoliate leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Manual collection/removal of gregarious larvae.
pests.biological_control: Spray Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki, Serotype H-39, 3b, Strain Z-52 @ 0.75-1.0 g/ha if RH >75% (2-3 small larvae/m row at early stage or 4-6 larvae at flowering).
pests.chemical_control: Apply Triazophos 40% EC @ 625 ml/ha or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 150 ml/ha for controlling defoliators
pests.dosage: Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki @ 0.75-1.0 g/ha; Triazophos 40% EC @ 625 ml/ha

pests.name: Pod borer (Helicoverpa)
pests.symptoms: Larvae feed on pods causing pod damage/yield loss.
pests.cultural_control: Install pheromone traps @ 10/ha with Helicoverpa armigera lure to monitor moth activity.
pests.biological_control: If 20-25 adult moths/trap observed, spray Ha NPV @ 100 LE/acre with one teaspoon indigo and sticker.
pests.chemical_control: Immediately spray Indoxacarb 15.8% EC @ 333 ml/ha for big larvae feeding on pods
pests.dosage: Ha NPV @ 100 LE/acre; Indoxacarb 15.8% EC @ 333 ml/ha

pests.name: White fly
pests.symptoms: Vector of Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV).
pests.cultural_control: Use YMV-resistant varieties.
pests.biological_control: Pupal parasitoids Encarsia formosa, Eretmocerus spp.
pests.chemical_control: Managed via seed treatment with Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 10 ml/ha to prevent whitefly transmission of YMV
pests.dosage: Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 10 ml/ha (seed treatment)

pests.name: Blue beetle
pests.symptoms: Adult beetles damage seedlings.
pests.cultural_control: Not specified beyond monitoring
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Spray Triazophos 40% EC @ 625 ml/ha when more than 4 adults/plant observed at seedling stage; repeat if population increases
pests.dosage: Triazophos 40% EC @ 625 ml/ha

diseases.name: Rust
diseases.symptoms: Pustules from flowering to pod-filling stage causing up to 30-100% yield loss; occurs in Maharashtra, Karnataka, MP, NE states, Kerala, Rajasthan, AP, Tamil Nadu.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified beyond general sanitation
diseases.biological_control: Three sprays of raw neem oil @ 1.0% at 30, 45, 60 DAS, or sprays of cow milk at 50/60/70 DAS, or seed soaking in cow urine (1:10) + asafoetida (0.01%) followed by sprays of cow urine at 50/60/70 DAS.
diseases.chemical_control: Two sprays of Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 100 ml/100 lit water for management of rust
diseases.dosage: Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 100 ml/100 l water (2 sprays); neem oil 1.0% (3 sprays at 30/45/60 DAS)

diseases.name: Yellow mosaic
diseases.symptoms: Yellow mosaic mottling from early vegetative to physiological maturity stage causing 15-75% yield loss; whitefly-transmitted.
diseases.cultural_control: Use YMV-resistant varieties (PK 416, PK 472, PS 564, PK 1024, PK 1029, PK 1042, Pusa 37, SL 295).
diseases.chemical_control: Managed via whitefly vector control - seed treatment Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 10 ml/ha
diseases.dosage: Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 10 ml/ha

diseases.name: Soybean mosaic
diseases.symptoms: Mosaic symptoms in late vegetative stage causing 25-50% yield loss.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified beyond resistant varieties
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Collar rot / Sclerotium blight
diseases.symptoms: Occurs 1-4 weeks after planting and mid-to-late flowering, causing 30-40% yield loss.
diseases.cultural_control: Rogue out collar-rot-affected seedlings.
diseases.biological_control: Seed soaking in mixture of cow urine (1:10) + asafoetida (0.01%) for 1 minute followed by two sprays of cow urine at 30 and 45 DAS, or seed soaking in cow urine (1:10) alone for 1 minute.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed via biological/cow-urine treatment
diseases.dosage: cow urine (1:10) + asafoetida (0.01%) seed soak + sprays at 30, 45 DAS

diseases.name: Charcoal rot

diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified beyond general sanitation/rotation
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Rhizoctonia root rot and aerial blight
diseases.symptoms: Root rot 1-4 weeks after planting; aerial blight during mid-flowering to pod formation following rain, causing up to 35% yield loss.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified

diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed via biological/cow-urine treatment
diseases.dosage: cow urine (1:10) + asafoetida (0.01%) seed soak + sprays at 30, 45 DAS

diseases.name: Bacterial pustule
diseases.symptoms: Symptoms from 35 days after sowing through the season, causing up to 20% yield loss.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified
diseases.biological_control: Seed soaking in mixture of cow urine (1:10) + asafoetida (0.01%), or in cow urine alone, for 1 minute.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed via biological/cow-urine treatment
diseases.dosage: cow urine (1:10) + asafoetida (0.01%) or plain cow urine, 1 minute seed soak

diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.scientific_name: Colletotrichum dematium f. sp. truncatum (Pers.) / Colletotrichum truncatum (Schwein.) Andrus & W.D. Moore
diseases.symptoms: Occurs throughout the season, causing 16-25% yield loss.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified
diseases.biological_control: Not specified beyond general cow-urine based treatments used for other diseases
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified
diseases.biological_control: Seed soaking in mixture of cow urine (1:10) + asafoetida (0.01%) for 1 minute, or above seed soaking followed by sprays of cow urine, or only sprays of cow milk at 30 and 45 DAS.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed via biological/cow-urine treatment
