Soyabean.general_safety_precautions: Do not spray if heavy rain is forecast within 1-2 days (reduces efficacy and increases runoff); spray operations for Spodoptera should be done in morning or late evening (larvae hide in soil crevices during the day), which also avoids harming parasitoids/predators; do not handle pheromone septa with bare hands, use clean cloth/cotton; same insecticide (e.g., Indoxacarb) should not be repeated for a second consecutive spray to manage resistance.
Soyabean.waiting_period_notes: No specific pre-harvest interval table captured in the extracted crop-stage section; general safety parameters annexure (Section 7.0) covers toxicity classification, WHO hazard class, and poisoning symptoms/first aid for the insecticides used (Triazophos, Chlorantraniliprole, Indoxacarb, Thiamethoxam, Fluchloralin, etc.).

Grapes.source_title: AESA based IPM package for Grapes (NIPHM)

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.scientific_name: Ferrisia virgata Cockerell, Maconellicoccus hirsutus, Pseudococcus spp.
pests.symptoms: Nymphs/adults suck sap from trunk, cordons, buds, spurs, leaves, shoots, and bunches; honeydew supports sooty mould making bunches unfit for market/raisins; can cause up to 100% loss in severe cases and death of young vines.
pests.cultural_control: Remove weeds/alternate host plants (hibiscus, okra, custard apple, guava); deep ploughing/raking in summer destroys nymphal stages; remove and destroy loose bark.
pests.biological_control: Release exotic predator Cryptolaemus montrouzieri @ 10 beetles/vine; neem-based emulsifiable formulations sprayed per azadirachtin concentration (50000 ppm @ 1 ml/l, 10000 ppm @ 2.5 ml/l, 3000 ppm @ 5 ml/l).
pests.chemical_control: Buprofezin 25% SC @ 400-600 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or methomyl 40% SP @ 500 g in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Buprofezin 25% SC @ 400-600 ml/200-400 l water/acre; methomyl 40% SP @ 500 g/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Flea beetle
pests.symptoms: Adults scrape sprouting buds after pruning causing failure to sprout; also feed on tender shoots/leaves/tendrils; larval damage on foliage.
pests.cultural_control: Remove loose bark at pruning to prevent egg laying; shake vines to dislodge beetles into kerosenated water (1:9) and destroy; put dry banana shred bundles on pruned ends to trap beetles overnight.
pests.biological_control: Neem-based emulsifiable formulations per azadirachtin concentration (as for mealybug).
pests.chemical_control: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 120-160 ml in 400 l water/acre or lambda-cyhalothrin 4.9% CS @ 100 g in 200-400 l water/acre or malathion 50% EC @ 400 ml in 600-800 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 120-160 ml/400 l water/acre; malathion 50% EC @ 400 ml/600-800 l water/acre

pests.name: Girdle beetle / grape cane girdler
pests.symptoms: Female girdles cane at two points around egg cavity; shoot beyond upper girdle bends over and drops, causing ragged 'pruned' appearance; little effect on crop unless close to fruit-bearing nodes.
pests.cultural_control: Cut and destroy infested shoots below lower girdle before adult emergence in summer; remove/destroy affected canes and dead wood during pruning.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Malathion 50% EC @ 400 ml in 600-800 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Malathion 50% EC @ 400 ml/600-800 l water/acre

pests.name: Thrips
pests.symptoms: Nymphs/adults rasp lower leaf surface producing speckled silvery effect; leaf curling under heavy incidence; berries develop corky brown layer reducing market price.
pests.cultural_control: Install 4-20 blue sticky traps/acre; deep ploughing/raking in summer; remove weeds/alternate hosts; collect/destroy damaged leaves, fruits, flowers.
pests.biological_control: Predatory mite (Amblyseius swirskii), predatory thrips (Aeolothrips spp.), anthocorid bug (Orius insidiosus).
pests.chemical_control: Emamectin benzoate 5% SG @ 88 g in 200-400 l water/acre or fipronil 80% WG @ 20-25 g in 300-400 l water/acre or lambda-cyhalothrin 4.9% CS @ 100 g in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Emamectin benzoate 5% SG @ 88 g/200-400 l water/acre; fipronil 80% WG @ 20-25 g/300-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Hoppers
pests.symptoms: Sap-sucking damage causing reduced vigor.
pests.cultural_control: Plant tall border crops (maize, sorghum, pearl millet); keep nursery weed-free; remove alternate host plants (hibiscus, okra, custard apple, guava).
pests.biological_control: Follow common biological practices (natural enemy conservation).
pests.chemical_control: Spray oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 400 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 400 ml/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Stem borer / cane borer
pests.symptoms: Grub bores into trunk/arms causing hollowing, drying/withering of affected branches; sawdust-like frass under vine indicates damage.
pests.cultural_control: Pierce infested plants with sharp needle/knife to kill caterpillar in stem; remove loose bark at pruning to prevent egg laying.
pests.biological_control: Predators: lacewing, coccinellids, King crow, dragonfly, spider, robber fly, praying mantis; parasitic nematode Ovomermis albicans.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed mechanically/culturally

pests.name: Leaf eating caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Gregarious young larvae scrape chlorophyll giving papery white appearance; later cause irregular holes and heavy defoliation/skeletonization.
pests.cultural_control: Grow castor as trap crop around vineyard for oviposition.
pests.biological_control: Spray NSKE 5% against eggs and first instar larvae; parasitoids Trichogramma chilonis, Telenomus spp. (egg), Campoletis chloridae, Peribea orbata, Carcelia sp (larval); predators Chrysoperla zastrowi sillemi, King crow, braconid wasps, dragonflies, spiders, praying mantids.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed beyond biological/NSKE control
pests.dosage: NSKE 5%

pests.name: Grape leaf folder
pests.symptoms: Larvae fold leaf and feed within, skeletonizing upper surface; heavy infestation gives patchy appearance to vine.
pests.cultural_control: Simple collection and burning of infested leaves.
pests.biological_control: Larval parasitoids Bracon cushmani, Cardiochiles spp.; predators lacewing, spider.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

pests.name: Red mites
pests.symptoms: Both nymphs and adults suck cell sap causing brown burnt patches; can delay bunch maturing/ripening and reduce sugar content.
pests.cultural_control: Proper irrigation scheduling reduces water stress and increases humidity, reducing mite population.
pests.biological_control: Predatory mites are the most efficient natural predators; also predatory beetles and spiders.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in crop-stage table beyond biological control

pests.name: Root-knot nematode
pests.symptoms: Galls on roots ('beard root' symptom); knobby/knotty roots; wilting during hot part of day especially under dry conditions; predisposes to fungal/bacterial root pathogens.
pests.cultural_control: Intercropping with marigold reduces nematode population; raise nursery in nematode-free/fumigated/solarized beds; apply decomposed poultry manure @ 200 g/sq m.
pests.biological_control: Not specified beyond general Trichoderma soil application
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Downy mildew
diseases.scientific_name: Plasmopara viticola (Berk. & Curt.) Berl. & de Toni
diseases.symptoms: Foliar and bunch infection reducing vigor and yield; favoured by humid conditions.
diseases.cultural_control: Prune vines after second week of October to minimize damage; remove and destroy affected portions at pruning; selectively collect and dispose infected leaves in compost pit.

diseases.dosage: See chemical_control field for full list of exact product rates

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on leaves/bunches; favoured by high humidity and poor air circulation.
diseases.cultural_control: Cultural practices reducing humidity, enabling good air circulation through canopy, and good light exposure; careful under-vine irrigation management (excess favours disease).
diseases.chemical_control: Benomyl 50% WP @ 120 g in 250-280 l water/acre or carbendazim 46.27% SC @ 0.1% (100 ml/100 l) in 100 l/acre or dinocap 48% EC @ 90 ml in 300 l water/acre or flusilazole 40% EC @ 0.01% or hexaconazole 2% SC @ 0.6-1.2 l in 200-300 l water/acre or hexaconazole 5% EC @ 200-400 ml in 200 l water/acre or kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC @ 240-280 ml in 200 l water/acre or lime sulphur 22% SC @ 1% (0.8-1 l/acre) or myclobutanil 10% WP @ 0.04% in 200 l/acre or penconazole 10% EC @ 50 ml/100 l water or sulphur 40% WP @ 1.2 Kg in 400 l water/acre or sulphur 55.16% SC @ 0.30% (300 ml/100 l water) or sulphur 80% WP @ 1-2 Kg in 300-400 l water/acre or sulphur 80% WG @ 0.75-1 Kg in 300-400 l water/acre or sulphur 85% DP @ 6-8 Kg/acre or triadimefon 25% WP @ 0.010% in 300 l water
diseases.dosage: See chemical_control field for full list of exact product rates

diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.symptoms: Leaf blight/anthracnose lesions with cankers on canes.
diseases.cultural_control: Irrigation by rose can; use resistant varieties (Bangalore Blue, Beauty Seedless, Bharat Early, Golden Queen, Large White); remove affected twigs/canes with cankers during pruning; burn or bury pruned material.
diseases.chemical_control: Aureofungin 46.15% w/v SP @ 0.005% in 300 l/acre or benomyl 50% WP @ 120 g in 250-280 l water/acre or carbendazim 50% WP @ 120 g in 240 l water/acre or chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 0.2% (200 g/100 l water)/acre or iprodione 50% WP @ 0.4-0.8 Kg in 200 l water/acre or kitazin 48% EC @ 0.20% (200 ml/200 l water) or mancozeb 75% WP @ 0.6-0.8 Kg in 300 l water/acre or ziram 80% WP @ 0.6-0.8 Kg in 300-400 l water/acre

diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.name: Botrytis bunch rot / gray mold
diseases.symptoms: Gray mold rot of bunches, worsened by humidity around clusters.

diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed; managed via handling/refrigeration

diseases.name: Blue mould rot / rhizopus rot (post-harvest)
diseases.symptoms: Post-harvest berry rot.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid injuries to ripe berries; inclusion of SO2-releasing pads while packing; remove diseased berries during grading; maintain cold storage between 40-10 degF (approx 4-12 degC).
diseases.chemical_control: Not applicable - managed via post-harvest handling/cold storage

Grapes.general_safety_precautions: Insecticide resistance management principles apply (P:D ratio >2:1 before spraying, rotate chemical classes, apply per label). Bird/bat deterrence covered under cultural practices (nets, noise makers, patrols) rather than chemical means.

pests.name: Cucurbit fruit fly
pests.scientific_name: Bactrocera cucurbitae, B. tau, B. dorsalis (Coquillett) (Tephritidae: Diptera)
pests.symptoms: Maggots damage fruit internally leading to rotting and fruit drop; national significance pest.
pests.cultural_control: Early maturing varieties less affected; change sowing dates; collect/destroy infested fruits; rake soil during/after fruiting to expose pupae; use methyl eugenol (0.1%) based traps.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoid Opius fletcheri (pupal); spray NSKE 5%.

pests.name: Pumpkin beetles (red pumpkin beetle)
pests.scientific_name: Raphidopalpa foveicollis, Aulacophora intermedia, A. cincta (Lucas) (Chrysomelidae: Coleoptera)
pests.symptoms: Adults/grubs feed on foliage and roots of seedlings.
pests.cultural_control: Deep summer ploughing exposes grubs and pupae.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predators such as Pennsylvania leather wing beetle (Chauliognathus pensylvanicus); parasitoid Celatoria setosa (grub); spray NSKE 5%.
pests.chemical_control: Apply trichlorfon 5% GR @ 200 g/acre or trichlorfon 5% DUST @ 200 g/acre

pests.name: Serpentine leaf miner
pests.symptoms: Larvae create serpentine mines in leaves reducing photosynthetic area.
pests.cultural_control: Change dates of sowing; grow castor, tomato or marigold as trap crop; use yellow sticky traps/cards @ 10/acre.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Tetrastichus ovularum (egg), Gronotoma micromorpha (larval/pupal), Diglyphus sp (larval), Opius phaseoli (pupal), Chrysocharis sp, Neochrysocharis formosa (larval); predators lacewings, lady beetles, spiders, fire ants; foliar spray NSKE 5%.

pests.dosage: NSKE 5%

pests.name: Aphids
pests.symptoms: Sap-sucking damage; vector of cucumber mosaic virus.
pests.cultural_control: Grow Lablab and mixed self-sowing annual/perennial flower species within cucurbits or as field boundary crops to attract beneficial insects.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Aphidius colemani, Diaeretiella spp., Aphelinus spp.; release 1st instar larvae of green lacewing (Chrysoperla carnea) @ 10,000/acre; conserve predators (anthocorid bugs, mirid bugs, syrphid flies, green lacewings, coccinellids, staphylinid beetle, Aphidoletis aphidimyza, Feltiella minuta).
pests.chemical_control: Spray imidacloprid 70% WG @ 14 g in 200 l water/acre
pests.dosage: imidacloprid 70% WG @ 14 g/200 l water/acre

pests.name: Pumpkin leaf caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Larval feeding on leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Not separately detailed beyond common practices
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

pests.name: Epilachna beetles
pests.symptoms: Grubs/adults skeletonize leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Not separately detailed beyond common practices
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed

diseases.symptoms: Vascular wilt of vines; national significance disease.
diseases.cultural_control: Use pathogen-free seeds; remove/destroy infected plants and debris; adopt crop rotation; avoid water stagnation, maintain proper drainage; use resistant varieties.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified beyond general Trichoderma/Pseudomonas soil application
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed culturally

diseases.scientific_name: Cercospora citrullina, C. melonis, C. lagenarium
diseases.symptoms: Leaf spots reducing photosynthetic area.

diseases.dosage: zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/300-400 l water/acre

diseases.scientific_name: Cucumber Mosaic Virus (Delhi, Haryana, Kerala, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh)
diseases.symptoms: Mosaic mottling of leaves; aphid-transmitted.

diseases.dosage: imidacloprid 70% WG @ 14 g/200 l water/acre

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.scientific_name: Erysiphe cichoracearum DC, Sphaerotheca fuliginea (Schltdl.) Pollacci
diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on leaves.

Turmeric.source_title: AESA based IPM package for Turmeric (NIPHM)

pests.name: Shoot borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into pseudostem/shoots causing wilting of central shoot.
pests.cultural_control: Grow ecological engineering (attractant) plants to conserve natural enemies; destroy infested shoots to kill harbouring caterpillars; light traps @ 1/acre (6-10 pm); mulch with green Lantana camara and Vitex negundo leaves @ 2 t/acre at 40 and 90 days after planting.

pests.chemical_control: This package emphasizes cultural and biological management for shoot borer; no specific synthetic insecticide dosage was captured in the crop-stage table
pests.dosage: Trichogramma chilonis @ 40,000/acre; neem oil 0.5% fortnightly

pests.name: Rhizome scale
pests.symptoms: Scale infestation on rhizomes reduces planting material quality.
pests.cultural_control: Collect and destroy severely infested rhizomes; select healthy rhizomes free from scale for sowing purpose.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Not specified in the crop-stage section (managed via sanitation and healthy seed selection)

pests.name: Rhizome fly
pests.symptoms: Maggots damage rotting rhizomes.
pests.cultural_control: Destroy stray plants in off season; select and plant healthy rhizomes; remove/destroy rotting rhizomes with maggots after harvest; intercrop with paddy reduces pest attack.
pests.biological_control: Conserve/inundate natural enemies (ladybird beetle, spiders, chrysopids, Trichogrammatids).
pests.chemical_control: Not specified

pests.name: Leaf roller / Bihar hairy caterpillar
pests.scientific_name: Udaspes folus Cramer (Lepidoptera: Hesperidae) - leaf roller/skipper
pests.symptoms: Larvae roll/feed on leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Collect/destroy egg masses and larvae; remove alternate weed hosts near field.
pests.biological_control: Conserve ladybird beetle, spiders, chrysopids, Bracon sp, fire ants, dragonfly, praying mantis, ground beetle, Trichogrammatids; release Trichogramma chilonis @ 20,000/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Not specified beyond biological control
pests.dosage: Trichogramma chilonis @ 20,000/acre

pests.name: Nematodes
pests.symptoms: Root infestation reducing rhizome yield.
pests.cultural_control: Uproot/destroy infested plants; treat infested rhizomes with hot water (50 degC) for 10 minutes; use nematode-free seed rhizomes; solarize beds for 40 days; intercrop marigold; deep ploughing/solarize infested fields; crop rotation with cereals, marigold, Chrysanthemum, Sesbania, Crotalaria spp., gaillardia, castor bean, Desmodium spp.
pests.biological_control: Extract of asafoetida, turmeric and water effective against several plant pathogens including nematodes; apply neem seed cake @ 100 Kg/acre before planting; Pochonia chlamydosporia (nematode biocontrol agent) incorporated @ 20 g/bed at 10^6 cfu/g at sowing.
pests.chemical_control: No synthetic nematicide specified; managed via cultural/biological measures
pests.dosage: Pochonia chlamydosporia @ 20 g/bed (10^6 cfu/g); neem cake @ 100 Kg/acre

diseases.name: Rhizome rot / soft rot
diseases.symptoms: Rotting of rhizomes reducing yield and storability.
diseases.cultural_control: Use resistant varieties; crop rotation with maize, cotton, soybean; plant disease-free seed rhizomes; use raised beds of 30 cm height; flooding treatment for 30 days or soil solarization during hottest months for 60 days; treat rhizomes with hot water at 51 degC for 10 minutes or clear polythene sheet solarization to 48 degC for 30 minutes; bio-fumigation using cabbage/mustard plant refuse.
diseases.biological_control: Plant flowering border plants (basil, marigold, fennel, sunflower) to attract biocontrol agents; apply pine needle and neem cake powder @ 100 Kg/acre (2 splits); apply oil cakes (neem, Calophyllum inophyllum, Pongamia glabra, Hibiscus sabdariffa, Brassica campestris) @ 0.8 tonnes/acre; foliar neem oil 0.5% twice at fortnightly interval; Fermented Plant Extract (garlic+onion leaves+cannabis+wild poisonous plant+cow urine+EM solution+rice wash extract+alcohol+water, 1:1:1:1:1:15) for seed treatment against soft rot, applied fortnightly up to July end.
diseases.chemical_control: No synthetic fungicide dosage captured; management is primarily cultural/biological in this package
diseases.dosage: hot water treatment @ 51 degC for 10 min; FPE seed treatment (1:1:1:1:1:15 ratio) fortnightly

diseases.name: Bacterial wilt
diseases.scientific_name: Ralstonia solanacearum (C. Martin and E.R. French) - regional
diseases.symptoms: Vascular wilt; sensitive to high (alkaline) soil pH.
diseases.cultural_control: Soil solarization for 60 days in summer; plant disease-free seed rhizomes; crop rotation with non-host crops (ragi, paddy, maize, sorghum); avoid rotation with tomato/potato/chillies/brinjal/peanut (hosts for R. solanacearum); rhizome hot water treatment at 47 degC for 3 minutes; bio-fumigation with cabbage/mustard refuse; avoid over/flood irrigation in affected areas.
diseases.chemical_control: Not specified (managed via sanitation/rotation/hot water treatment)
diseases.dosage: rhizome hot water treatment @ 47 degC for 3 minutes

diseases.name: Leaf spot
diseases.symptoms: Leaf spot lesions reducing photosynthetic area.
diseases.cultural_control: Pluck/remove infested leaves and uproot/destroy infested plants; use proper green mulching to reduce soil splash.
diseases.biological_control: Plant extracts such as garlic extract effective against foliar pathogens; spray extract of asafoetida, turmeric and water.
diseases.chemical_control: Not specified - managed via plant-extract based biological control

diseases.name: Leaf blotch
diseases.symptoms: Blotch lesions on leaves.
diseases.cultural_control: Use proper green mulching to reduce soil splash; field sanitation; crop rotation with cereal/legume crops.
diseases.biological_control: Plant extracts such as garlic extract effective against foliar pathogens.
diseases.chemical_control: Not specified

Turmeric.general_safety_precautions: This package emphasizes biointensive/organic-leaning practices (neem cake, plant extracts, Fermented Plant Extract, hot water/solarization treatment of rhizomes) over synthetic chemical pesticides; general insecticide resistance management principles (rotate modes of action, apply per label, use as last resort) still apply where synthetic products are used.
Turmeric.waiting_period_notes: No specific pre-harvest interval table was captured for turmeric in the extracted sections; harvested rhizomes should be stored pest/disease-free in shaded pits lined with sand/sawdust and covered with coconut fronds, discarding any soft-rot/bacterial-rot infected rhizomes before storage.

Citrus.source_title: AESA based IPM package for Citrus (NIPHM)

pests.name: Citrus aphid
pests.symptoms: Feeds on tender foliage/flowers; transmits Citrus Tristeza Virus; nymphs/adults suck sap causing wilting, flower dropping; infested leaves become cup-shaped and crinkled; growth is hindered.
pests.cultural_control: Not separately specified beyond general orchard sanitation
pests.biological_control: Conserve/enhance predators - lacewings, birds, earwigs, ground beetles, rove beetles, spiders; use yellow sticky traps.
pests.chemical_control: Foliar spray with dimethoate 30% EC @ 594-792 ml in 600-800 l water/acre or chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 600-800 ml in 600-800 l water/acre or monocrotophos 36% SL @ 600-800 ml in 200-800 l water/acre or oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 480-640 ml in 600-800 l water/acre
pests.dosage: dimethoate 30% EC @ 594-792 ml/600-800 l water/acre; chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 600-800 ml/600-800 l water/acre

pests.name: Citrus psylla
pests.symptoms: Vector of citrus greening (Huanglongbing) disease; nymphs/adults damage new flush.
pests.cultural_control: Collect and destroy infested plant parts.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Tamarixia radiata, Diaphorencyrtus aligarhensis; predators Chrysoperla zastrowi sillemi, coccinellids, syrphids.
pests.chemical_control: Systemic insecticide imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 50 ml (dose depends on tree size/equipment); foliar spray thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 40 g in 400 l water/acre or oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 600-800 ml in 600-800 l water/acre; control psyllids with dimethoate or imidacloprid
pests.dosage: imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 50 ml (per tree, size-dependent); thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 40 g/400 l water/acre

pests.name: Citrus leaf miner
pests.symptoms: Larvae mine new flush leaves causing distortion and reduced vigor.
pests.cultural_control: Pheromone traps @ 5/acre; pruning of affected parts during winter and burning.
pests.biological_control: Not specified beyond general natural enemy conservation
pests.chemical_control: Carbofuran 3% CG @ 20,000 g/acre or foliar spray imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 50 ml (size-dependent) or permethrin 25% EC @ 160-240 ml in 400 l water/acre or phorate 10% CG @ 6,000 g/acre
pests.dosage: Carbofuran 3% CG @ 20,000 g/acre; permethrin 25% EC @ 160-240 ml/400 l water/acre; phorate 10% CG @ 6,000 g/acre

pests.name: Mealybug
pests.symptoms: Sap-sucking colonies on shoots/stems.
pests.cultural_control: Prune affected shoots in winter; destroy ant colonies; grow attractant plants (Bachelor's Buttons/cornflower, coriander) to attract natural enemy wasps.
pests.biological_control: Field release of Australian ladybird beetle (Cryptolaemus montrouzieri) @ 10 beetles/tree.
pests.chemical_control: Fish oil rosin soap 25 g/l or spray methyl demeton or dimethoate 2 ml/l or confidor 200 SL @ 4 ml/acre
pests.dosage: fish oil rosin soap @ 25 g/l; dimethoate @ 2 ml/l; confidor 200 SL @ 4 ml/acre

pests.name: Fruit sucking moth
pests.symptoms: Adults puncture ripening fruit to feed on juice causing rot/drop.
pests.cultural_control: Destroy larval alternate hosts around orchards; collect/destroy rotten and dropped fruits; collect/destroy moths at night with torch; install fluorescent light trap (1/acre) one month before fruit maturation, 7-11 pm.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Not specified (managed via mechanical/light trap control)

pests.name: Citrus/Lemon butterfly
pests.symptoms: Larvae defoliate young citrus leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Grow attractant plants (carrot family, sunflower family, buckwheat, alfalfa, corn, nectar-rich plants).
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Trichogramma evanescens, Telenomus spp. (eggs), Brachymeria spp., Cotesia (larvae), Pterolus sp. (pupae); hand-pick larvae and destroy.
pests.chemical_control: Spray Malathion @ 1 ml/l or foliar spray with quinalphos 25% EC @ 600-800 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: Malathion @ 1 ml/l; quinalphos 25% EC @ 600-800 ml/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Citrus mite
pests.symptoms: Aggravated by water stress especially in late summer.
pests.cultural_control: Ensure trees are well-irrigated, particularly during late-summer stress periods.
pests.biological_control: Predacious mite Euseius hibisci, and predators Agistemus sp., Amblyseius hibisci.
pests.chemical_control: Foliar spray with monocrotophos 36% SL @ 374.8-500 ml in 200-800 l water/acre
pests.dosage: monocrotophos 36% SL @ 374.8-500 ml/200-800 l water/acre

pests.name: Scale insects
pests.symptoms: Colonies on twigs/leaves reducing tree vigor.
pests.cultural_control: Pruning scale-infested twigs; control ants and dust (competitive advantage for scale); field release of Vedalia and Australian ladybugs.
pests.biological_control: Spray dormant oil in late winter before spring; horticultural oil year-round if needed; manure compost tea + molasses + citrus oil mixture; garlic-pepper tea.
pests.chemical_control: Foliar spray with quinalphos 25% EC @ 1680-2240 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: quinalphos 25% EC @ 1680-2240 ml/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Citrus blackfly
pests.symptoms: Nymphs and adults damage leaves; sooty mould from honeydew.
pests.cultural_control: Collect/destroy damaged plant parts with nymphs/pupae/adults; use light trap (550 nm wavelength); yellow sticky traps/cards.
pests.biological_control: Pupal parasitoids Encarsia formosa, Eretmocerus spp.; predators Chrysoperla zastrowi sillemi, coccinellids, spiders.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed via biological/mechanical control

pests.name: Citrus nematode
pests.symptoms: Root infestation reducing vigor and yield.
pests.cultural_control: Deep summer ploughing to control nematodes and soil-borne diseases; use resistant/tolerant rootstocks.
pests.biological_control: Not specified
pests.chemical_control: Not specified in the crop-stage section

diseases.name: Citrus scab
diseases.symptoms: Scab-like corky lesions on leaves/fruit surface.
diseases.cultural_control: Collect and destroy infested leaves, twigs and fruits.
diseases.chemical_control: Spray with 0.3% COC (copper oxychloride) or 1.0% Bordeaux mixture or 0.2% chlorothalonil at 15-day interval
diseases.dosage: 0.3% COC or 1.0% Bordeaux mixture or 0.2% chlorothalonil, 15-day interval

diseases.name: Citrus canker
diseases.symptoms: Corky raised lesions on leaves, stems and fruit.
diseases.cultural_control: Select canker-free seedlings for planting; prune out and burn all canker-infected twigs before monsoon; maintain proper aeration via training/pruning to reduce leaf wetness.
diseases.chemical_control: Captan 75% WP @ 666.8 g in 6-8 l water/acre; (streptomycin sulphate 9% + tetracycline hydrochloride 1%) SP spray (streptocycline) @ 50-100 ppm solution repeated at 15-20 day interval after appearance of new growth; cover foliage and young fruits fully
diseases.dosage: Captan 75% WP @ 666.8 g/6-8 l water/acre; streptocycline 50-100 ppm, repeated at 15-20 day interval

diseases.name: Citrus tristeza disease
diseases.symptoms: Vascular decline; aphid-transmitted, causes secondary spread in orchards.
diseases.cultural_control: Use certified budwood free of CTV; remove diseased trees when noticed; fresh plantings with virus-free material on tolerant rootstocks; avoid susceptible rootstocks for sweet orange/mandarin.
diseases.chemical_control: For acid lime use seedlings immunized with mild strain of CTV (cross protection); periodic sprays of Monocrotophos 0.05% control citrus aphid vector reducing secondary spread; copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 1 Kg in 300-400 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: Monocrotophos 0.05%; copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 1 Kg/300-400 l water/acre

diseases.name: Gummosis
diseases.symptoms: Gum exudation from bark; disease spreads via infected bark tissue.
diseases.cultural_control: Remove diseased bark and a buffer strip of healthy bark around infection margins; site selection with adequate drainage; use resistant rootstocks; avoid water contact with trunk (ring irrigation method).
diseases.chemical_control: Aureofungin 46.15% w/v SP @ 300 (1%) g/ml/acre
diseases.dosage: Aureofungin 46.15% SP @ 1% (300 g or ml/acre)

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.symptoms: White powdery growth on leaves; encouraged by dense leafy growth from excess nitrogen.
diseases.cultural_control: Apply nitrogen fertilizer at precise, lower rates (less than 0.03175 metric ton/acre) to decrease severity.
diseases.chemical_control: Sulphur 80% WP @ 1252 g in 300-400 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: Sulphur 80% WP @ 1252 g/300-400 l water/acre

diseases.name: Greasy spot
diseases.symptoms: Greasy-appearing spots on leaves.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified
diseases.chemical_control: Zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300-400 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: Zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/300-400 l water/acre

diseases.name: Brown rot
diseases.symptoms: Fruit rot.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified
diseases.chemical_control: Captan 75% WP @ 500 g in 6-8 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: Captan 75% WP @ 500 g/6-8 l water/acre

diseases.name: Citrus greening (Huanglongbing)
diseases.symptoms: Vascular decline transmitted by citrus psylla vector.
diseases.cultural_control: Site selection with adequate drainage; high budding (30-46 cm or above); provide inner ring ~45 cm around trunk to prevent moist soil (double-ring irrigation); avoid irrigation water contact with trunk; avoid injuries to crown roots/stem base; use resistant sour orange rootstocks; use certified pathogen-free budwood.
diseases.chemical_control: Control psyllid vector with insecticides like dimethoate or imidacloprid; apply Bordeaux paste or ZnSO4+CuSO4+lime (5:1:4) to ~60 cm height above ground at least once a year
diseases.dosage: Bordeaux paste ZnSO4:CuSO4:lime (5:1:4 ratio)

Citrus.general_safety_precautions: Insecticide resistance management principles apply (P:D ratio >2:1 before spraying, rotate chemical classes/modes of action, apply per label rates/timing).
Citrus.waiting_period_notes: Note explicitly states pesticide dosages/spray fluid volumes are based on high-volume sprayer application. No separate crop-specific pre-harvest interval table was captured in the extracted sections.

Okra.source_title: AESA based IPM package for Okra (NIPHM)

pests.name: Okra shoot and fruit borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into shoots and fruits causing wilting of shoots and damaged/unmarketable fruits.
pests.cultural_control: Collect/destroy affected fruits; avoid growing malvaceous crops in sequence; clip/nip off shoots below entrance hole; pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre for monitoring.
pests.biological_control: Spray azadirachtin 0.03% (300 ppm) neem oil WSP @ 1000-2000 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or azadirachtin 5% W/W neem extract @ 80 ml in 160 l water/acre; spray B.t. var gallariae @ 400-600 g in 200 l water/acre; release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 40,000/acre and predator Chrysoperla carnea (1st instar) @ 4,000/acre; spray Beauveria bassiana 1% WP @ 1500-2000 g in 160-200 l water/acre; apply EPNs @ 250 crore infective juveniles of Steinernema feltiae/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Foliar spray with chloranthraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 50 ml in 200 l water/acre or cypermethrin 10% EC @ 220-304 ml in 60-160 l water/acre or cypermethrin 25% EC @ 60-80 ml in 200 l water/acre or fenpropathrin 30% EC @ 100-136 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or deltamethrin 2.8% EC @ 160-240 ml in 160-240 l water/acre or emamectin benzoate 5% SG @ 54-68 g in 200 l water/acre or fenvalerate 20% EC @ 120-150 ml in 240-300 l water/acre or lambda cyhalothrin 4.9% CS @ 120 ml in 200 l water/acre or permethrin 25% EC @ 160-200 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or pyridalyl 10% EC @ 200-300 ml in 200-300 l water/acre or quinalphos 20% AF @ 500-600 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or pyriproxyfen 5% + fenpropathrin 15% EC @ 200-300 ml in 200-300 l water/acre or carbaryl 50% WP @ 800 g in 200-400 l water/acre or lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC @ 120 ml in 120-160 l water/acre or malathion 50% EC @ 600 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or phosalone 35% EC @ 500 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or quinalphos 25% EC @ 320 ml in 200-400 l water
pests.dosage: See chemical_control field for full list of exact product rates

pests.name: Whitefly (Yellow vein mosaic vector)
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking and vector of Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus.
pests.cultural_control: Field sanitation/roguing; plant tall border crops (maize/sorghum/pearl millet, 4 rows); yellow sticky traps @ 2/acre; peppermint as repellent; grow tolerant varieties; rain-bird type irrigation.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predators coccinellids, lacewings, spiders, Dicyphus hesperus; parasitoids Encarsia sp, Eretmocerus spp., Chrysocharis pentheus; release Chrysoperla carnea @ 8,000 larvae/acre; spray NSKE 5% or azadirachtin 0.03% neem oil WSP @ 1000-2000 ml in 200-400 l water/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Spray oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 400 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or fenpropathrin 30% EC @ 100-136 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 40 g in 200-400 l water/acre or pyriproxyfen 5% + fenpropathrin 15% EC @ 200-300 ml in 200-300 l water/acre
pests.dosage: oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 400 ml/200-400 l water/acre; thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 40 g/200-400 l water/acre

pests.name: Jassids / Leafhoppers
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking causes leaf hopper-burn symptoms.
pests.cultural_control: Destroy alternate host plants; use resistant varieties; okra intercropped with baby corn reduces pre-spray leafhopper population.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predators Distina albina, Chrysoperla spp.; parasitoid Lymaenon empoascae (egg); spray NSKE 5% or azadirachtin formulations.
pests.chemical_control: Seed treatment with imidacloprid 48% FS @ 500-900 ml/100 kg seed or imidacloprid 70% WS @ 500-1000 ml/100 kg seed; spray thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 40 g in 200-400 l water/acre or cypermethrin 25% EC @ 60-80 ml in 200 l water/acre or fenvalerate 20% EC @ 120-150 ml in 240-300 l water/acre or imidacloprid 70% WG @ 12-14 g in 150-200 l water/acre or imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 40 ml in 200 l water/acre or permethrin 25% EC @ 160-200 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or carbaryl 5% DP @ 8000 g/acre or carbofuran 3% CG @ 13320 g/acre or deltamethrin 2.8% EC @ 160-240 ml in 160-240 l water/acre or dimethoate 30% EC @ 792 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or malathion 50% EC @ 500 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or oxydemeton-methyl 25% EC @ 640 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or quinalphos 25% EC @ 400 ml in 200-400 l water
pests.dosage: imidacloprid 48% FS @ 500-900 ml/100 kg seed; see chemical_control for spray rates

pests.name: Aphids
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking damage causing leaf curling/stunting.
pests.cultural_control: Not separately specified beyond common practices
pests.biological_control: Conserve wasps, green lacewings, earwigs, ground beetles, rove beetles, spiders, coccinellids, syrphids; spray azadirachtin 5% W/W neem extract @ 80 ml in 160 l water/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Seed treatment with imidacloprid 48% FS @ 500-900 ml/100 kg seed or imidacloprid 70% WS @ 500-1000 ml/100 kg seed; spray acetamiprid 20% SP @ 30 g in 200-240 l water/acre or imidacloprid 70% WG @ 12-14 g in 150-200 l water/acre or imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 40 ml in 200 l water/acre or permethrin 25% EC @ 160-200 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or malathion 50% EC @ 400 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or thiamethoxam 70% WS @ 286 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 40 g in 200-400 l water/acre or dimethoate 30% EC @ 924 ml in 200-400 l water/acre
pests.dosage: See chemical_control field for exact rates

pests.name: Mites
pests.scientific_name: Red spider mite: Tetranychus spp. (Acarina: Tetranychidae)
pests.symptoms: Cell sap removal causes stippling and leaf drying.
pests.cultural_control: Grow nurseries away from infested crops; avoid nutrient/water stress; mulch and organic matter to improve water holding; keep pigeon pea hedges to encourage predatory mites; uproot/burn infested plants early; keep field weed-free; remove/burn infested residue after harvest.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predators - anthocorid bugs, mirid bugs, syrphid/hover flies, green lacewings, predatory mites (Amblyseius alstoniae, A. womersleyi, A. fallacies, Phytoseiulus persimilis), coccinellid beetle (Stethorus punctillum), staphylinid beetles, cecidomyiid, gall midge (Feltiella minuta).
pests.chemical_control: Spray dicofol 18.5% EC @ 540-1080 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or fenazaquin 10% EC @ 500 ml in 200 l water/acre or fenpropathrin 30% EC @ 100-136 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 160-200 ml in 200 l water/acre or quinalphos 25% EC @ 400 ml in 200-400 l water
pests.dosage: dicofol 18.5% EC @ 540-1080 ml/200-400 l water/acre; see chemical_control for other rates

pests.name: Gram pod borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae feed on flowers/pods.
pests.cultural_control: Field sanitation/roguing; Ocimum/Basil as repellent; light traps @ 1/acre; bird perches @ 40/acre; ovipositional trap crop marigold @ 100 plants/acre; pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre (ETL 10 moths/trap/day).
pests.biological_control: Spray NSKE 5% or azadirachtin formulations; spray NPV @ 250 LE/acre with jaggery 1 kg, sandovit 100 ml or Robin Blue 50 g, thrice at 10-15 day interval; conserve parasitoids Trichogramma chilonis, Tetrastichus spp., Chelonus spp., Telenomus spp., Netelia product, Carcelia spp., Campoletis chlorideae, Bracon spp.; conserve predators Chrysoperla carnea, coccinellids, king crow, wasp, dragonfly, spider, robber fly, reduviid bug, praying mantis; spray Beauveria bassiana 1% WP @ 1500-2000 g in 160-200 l water/acre; spray B.t. var gallariae @ 400-600 g in 200 l water/acre; conserve parasitic nematode Ovomermis albicans.
pests.chemical_control: Foliar spray with chloranthraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 50 ml in 200 l water/acre or cypermethrin 10% EC @ 220-304 ml in 60-160 l water/acre or cypermethrin 25% EC @ 60-80 ml in 200 l water/acre or emamectin benzoate 5% SG @ 54-68 g in 200 l water/acre or fenpropathrin 30% EC @ 100-136 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or fenvalerate 20% EC @ 120-150 ml in 240-300 l water/acre or lambda cyhalothrin 4.9% CS @ 120 ml in 200 l water/acre or permethrin 25% EC @ 160-200 ml in 400 l water/acre or pyridalyl 10% EC @ 200-300 ml in 200-300 l water/acre or quinalphos 20% AF @ 500-600 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or carbaryl 50% WP @ 800 g in 200-400 l water/acre or deltamethrin 2.8% EC @ 160-240 ml in 160-240 l water/acre or phosalone 35% EC @ 500 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or quinalphos 25% EC @ 320 ml in 200-400 l water
pests.dosage: NPV @ 250 LE/acre; see chemical_control field for exact synthetic pesticide rates

diseases.name: Damping off
diseases.symptoms: Seedling collapse in nursery.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid excessive watering/poorly drained field areas; raised beds.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified beyond general Trichoderma seed/soil treatment
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the extracted crop-stage section

diseases.name: Yellow vein mosaic disease
diseases.symptoms: Yellow vein-clearing mosaic symptoms transmitted by whitefly.
diseases.cultural_control: Grow tolerant varieties; use border crops and repellent plants as under whitefly management.
diseases.biological_control: Managed via whitefly vector biological control
diseases.chemical_control: Managed via whitefly vector control - see chemical control listed under Whitefly

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on leaves.
diseases.cultural_control: Monitor adjacent fields for infection; maintain proper plant spacing to reduce relative humidity.
diseases.biological_control: Spray azadirachtin 0.03% (300 ppm) neem oil EC @ 800-1000 ml in 200 l water/acre.
diseases.chemical_control: Spray sulphur 80% WP @ 1252 g in 300-400 l water/acre or dinocap 48% EC @ 90 ml in 300 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: sulphur 80% WP @ 1252 g/300-400 l water/acre; dinocap 48% EC @ 90 ml/300 l water/acre

diseases.name: Cercospora leaf spot
diseases.symptoms: Leaf spot lesions reducing photosynthetic area.
diseases.cultural_control: Removal and proper disposal/burning of infected leaves.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in this package section

Okra.general_safety_precautions: Insecticide resistance management: use insecticides as last resort with P:D ratio >2:1; rotate insecticide classes/modes of action; avoid broad-spectrum products where narrow-spectrum will work.
Okra.waiting_period_notes: No crop-specific pre-harvest interval table captured for okra in the extracted sections; general safety-parameters annexure of the NIPHM series covers toxicity/first-aid guidance for the insecticides listed (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam, dimethoate, malathion, quinalphos, etc.).

Brinjal.source_title: AESA based IPM package for Brinjal (NIPHM)

pests.name: Fruit and shoot borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into shoots (causing wilting) and fruits (making them unmarketable).
pests.cultural_control: Avoid continuous brinjal-potato cultivation in same area; use resistant varieties; intercrop brinjal (2 rows) with coriander/fennel (1 row); pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre monitoring, 10/acre mass trapping from 20 DAT; promptly remove/destroy infested shoots and fruit.
pests.biological_control: Release Trichogramma chilonis @ 20,000/acre/week from 21 days after transplanting till end of crop; conserve predators Campyloneura sp, Cheilomenes sexmaculata, Coccinella septempunctata, Brumoides suturalis, C. carnea; conserve parasitoids Pseudoperichaeta sp, Phanerotoma sp, Itamoplex sp, Eriborus argenteopilosus, Diadegma apostate, Pristomerus testaceus, Trathala flavo-orbitalis, Bracon greeni; spray azadirachtin 1% EC @ 400-600 ml in 400 l water/acre or azadirachtin 0.03% WSP @ 1000-2000 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or NSKE 5%; apply EPNs @ 1.0 crore infective juveniles of Steinernema glaseri/acre.

pests.name: Epilachna (Hadda) beetle
pests.symptoms: Grubs and adults skeletonize leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Hand-pick and destroy insects visible on skeletonized leaves.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Pediobius foveolatus (nymphal), Chrysocharis johnsoni (nymphal), Tetrastichus ovularum (egg), Uga menoni (larval); predators Eocanthecona furcellata, Rhinocoris fuscipes; spray NSKE 5%.

pests.name: Jassids
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking; vector of brinjal little leaf phytoplasma disease.
pests.cultural_control: Grow okra as trap crop; remove affected parts.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Lymaenon empoascae, Anagrus flaveolus, Stethynium triclavatum; predators ladybird beetles, green lacewings; spray NSKE 5%.
pests.chemical_control: Apply phorate 10% CG @ 6000 g/acre or spray phosphamidon 40% SL @ 250-300 ml in 200 l water/acre or quinalphos 25% EC @ 400 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or quinalphos 20% AF @ 600-700 ml in 300-400 l water or thiometon 25% EC @ 400 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or betacyfluthrin 8.49% + imidacloprid 19.81% OD @ 70-80 ml in 200 l water/acre or carbaryl 50% WP @ 800 g in 200-400 l water/acre or cypermethrin 25% EC @ 60-80 ml in 200 l water/acre or deltamethrin 1% + triazophos 35% EC @ 400-500 ml in 200 l water/acre
pests.dosage: phorate 10% CG @ 6000 g/acre; phosphamidon 40% SL @ 250-300 ml/200 l water/acre

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking and honeydew-related sooty mould; potential virus vector.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural/mechanical practices as for other sucking pests.
pests.biological_control: Conserve natural enemies as for aphids/jassids.
pests.chemical_control: Same chemical options as jassid/aphid control listed

pests.name: Aphids
pests.symptoms: Sap sucking causing curling/stunting.
pests.cultural_control: Not separately specified beyond common practices
pests.biological_control: Release 1st instar larvae of green lacewing (Chrysoperla carnea) @ 4,000/acre; conserve parasitoids Aphidius colemani, Diaeretiella spp., Aphelinus spp.; predators ladybird beetles (Coccinella septempunctata, Menochilus sexmaculata).

pests.dosage: phorate 10% CG @ 6000 g/acre; phosphamidon 40% SL @ 250-300 ml/300 l water/acre

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.symptoms: Cell sap removal from leaves.
pests.cultural_control: Grow nurseries away from infested crops; avoid water/nutrient stress; mulch; maintain perennial hedges (pigeon pea) to encourage predatory mites; uproot/burn infested plants early; keep field weed-free; remove/burn infested residue after harvest.
pests.biological_control: Conserve green lacewings, predatory mites (Amblyseius alstoniae, A. womersleyi, A. fallacies, Phytoseiulus persimilis), coccinellid beetles (Stethorus punctillum), staphylinid beetles, cecidomyiid fly, gall midge (Feltiella minuta); spray NSKE 5%.
pests.chemical_control: Spray fenazaquin 10% EC @ 500 ml in 200 l water/acre or fenpropathrin 30% EC @ 100-136 ml in 300-400 l water/acre or dicofol 18.5% EC @ 540-1080 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or malathion 50% EC @ 600 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or flumite/flufenzinzine 20% SC @ 160-200 ml in 200-400 l water/acre or propargite 57% EC @ 400 ml in 160 l water/acre or spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 160 ml in 200 l water/acre or phorate 10% CG @ 6000 g/acre
pests.dosage: See chemical_control field for exact rates

pests.name: Stem borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into stems.
pests.cultural_control: Avoid ratooning brinjal crop; uproot/burn infested plants before planting new crop.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Pristomerus euzopherae.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the crop-stage table

diseases.name: Damping off
diseases.symptoms: Seedling collapse in nursery under excess moisture.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid excessive watering/poorly drained areas; use raised beds >15 cm height; plug tray method with sterilized potting mixture.
diseases.biological_control: Nursery treatment: mix 250 g Trichoderma viride 1.0% WP in 50 l water and drench soil in 400 sq m area; seed treatment with Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 5 g/kg seed; seedling root-dip treatment (10 g Trichoderma viride 1% WP in 1 l water, dip 15 minutes); soil treatment mixing 1.0 kg Trichoderma viride 1% WP with 25 kg FYM per acre.
diseases.chemical_control: Soil drench with captan 75% WP @ 1000 g in 400 l water/acre (nursery)
diseases.dosage: Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 5 g/kg seed; captan 75% WP @ 1000 g/400 l water/acre (nursery drench)

diseases.name: Bacterial wilt
diseases.symptoms: Vascular wilt.
diseases.cultural_control: Grow resistant varieties; crop rotation with non-solanaceous hosts (maize, soybean, wheat, rice, gingelly) and green manuring; green manuring with Brassica sp (biofumigation); soil solarization with transparent 125 micron polyethylene sheet for 8-10 weeks (March-June) in nurseries.
diseases.biological_control: Use neem cake; mix 1 kg Trichoderma viride 1% WP with 25 kg FYM per acre, broadcast and irrigate immediately.
diseases.chemical_control: Not separately dosed - managed via biological/cultural measures

diseases.name: Phomopsis blight (fruit rot)
diseases.symptoms: Blight and fruit rot.
diseases.cultural_control: Procure seeds from healthy fruits, hot water treatment of seed at 50 degC for 30 minutes; avoid continuous brinjal cultivation; rotate with non-solanaceous crops (paddy-gingelly); summer deep ploughing reduces initial inoculum; remove/destroy diseased crop debris; use resistant varieties.
diseases.chemical_control: Spray zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300-400 l water/acre or carbendazim 50% WP @ 120 g in 240 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g/300-400 l water/acre; carbendazim 50% WP @ 120 g/240 l water/acre

diseases.name: Little leaf of brinjal
diseases.symptoms: Little-leaf symptom with proliferation of small leaves; transmitted by jassid vector.
diseases.cultural_control: Destroy affected plants in early stages; eradicate solanaceous weed hosts; plant tolerant varieties.
diseases.chemical_control: Managed via vector (jassid/leaf hopper) control by spraying insecticides listed under jassid control

diseases.name: Alternaria and Cercospora leaf spot
diseases.scientific_name: Alternaria melongenae Rangaswami & Samb. / Alternaria spp.; Cercospora solani f.sp. melongenae Feuilleaub / Cercospora melongena
diseases.symptoms: Leaf spot lesions reducing photosynthetic area.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified beyond field sanitation
diseases.chemical_control: Spray carbendazim 50% WP @ 120 g in 240 l water/acre
diseases.dosage: carbendazim 50% WP @ 120 g/240 l water/acre

diseases.name: Root-knot nematode
diseases.symptoms: Root galling reducing plant vigor.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately specified beyond general soil management
diseases.biological_control: In main field, apply 2 tons FYM enriched with 100-200 kg neem or pongamia cake.
diseases.chemical_control: Apply carbofuran 3% CG @ 26,640 g/acre
diseases.dosage: carbofuran 3% CG @ 26,640 g/acre

Brinjal.general_safety_precautions: Termite management: locate termitarium, dig out queen and destroy (only permanent remedy); fumigate ant hill with carbon disulphide/chloroform mixture; destroy crop residues that harbor infestation. Mealybug: remove/burn crop residues in previously infested fields; conserve coccinellid predators (Cryptolaemus montrouzieri, Cheilomenes sexmaculata, Rodolia fumida, Scymnus coccivora, Nephus regularis); use soap oil or fish oil resin soap twice at 15-20 day interval. Brinjal lace bug controlled via crop rotation and natural predators (lady beetles, spiders, shield bugs).
Brinjal.waiting_period_notes: No crop-specific pre-harvest interval table was captured for brinjal in the extracted sections; standard practice per NIPHM series is to avoid pesticide application in the final days before harvest and to follow label pre-harvest intervals for each product listed above.
